By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 19 Nov 2026 16:04, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:37.

Lille will be looking to strengthen their position in the Ligue 1 title race when they welcome Lyon to the Stade Pierre-Mauroy on Saturday evening for matchday 11 action.

The hosts sit second in the Ligue 1 table with 21 points from their opening 10 matches, two behind leaders Paris Saint-Germain, while the fifth-placed visitors have 17 points and will be hoping to close the gap on their opponents in Carlos Vicens's first game in charge.

Lille head into the weekend in encouraging form after winning their last two league outings, beating Lens 1-0 before claiming a 2-1 victory away to Rennes prior to the international break, where Nathan Ngoy's second-half goal proved decisive.

Davide Ancelotti will be particularly pleased with how his side have rediscovered their rhythm after consecutive draws against Brest and Monaco derailed the Mastiffs' title charge, with the northern French outfit having lost just once in their opening 10 Ligue 1 fixtures (W6, D3).

Much of Lille's success this season has been built on their defensive solidity, with seven goals conceded representing the best record in the division, while five clean sheets leave them behind only Lorient (six) in that regard.

Les Dogues have also found the net in every league outing this season, although they have scored more than once in just 40% of their 10 top-flight matches, including two of their five fixtures on their own turf.

Nevertheless, Lille have been reliable at the Stade Pierre-Mauroy, winning three of their five Ligue 1 games at the ground and avoiding defeat in the other two to boast the division's fifth-best home record.

Victory on Saturday would not only strengthen the hosts' position in the standings but also provide a timely confidence boost ahead of Wednesday's Champions League meeting with Bayern Munich, with the Mastiffs currently second from bottom in the league phase table after collecting just one point from their opening four continental fixtures.

Vicens will also have one eye on next Thursday’s home meeting with Lillstrom in the Europa League, where Lyon sit 13th in the 36-team table after picking up seven points from their first four matches.

However, the Spanish coach's immediate priority will be to get his new side back to winning ways following a 2-0 defeat at Brest in Lyon's most recent league outing, which came under interim boss Jorge Maciel following the departure of Paolo Fonseca for Sporting Lisbon.

That setback further highlighted Lyon's struggles on the road, having now lost their last three Ligue 1 away matches while conceding exactly two goals in each of those outings, with their only victory in five domestic trips this season coming against Toulouse on the opening weekend.

Nevertheless, a superior head-to-head record should offer the visitors some encouragement ahead of Saturday's contest, considering Lyon have won six of their last seven meetings across all competitions (D1) with Lille, including 1-0 victories in both league encounters last season.

Lille remain without Tiago Santos, who is expected to miss the remainder of the season after rupturing his cruciate ligament, while Hamza Igamane is also unavailable as he continues his recovery from an ACL injury, although a return is expected in December.

Ayase Ueda is doubtful after sustaining a plantar fascia injury, with the forward having resumed running but yet to return to full training, although Ancelotti previously suggested that the Japanese attacker could be available for this fixture.

Hakon Arnar Haraldsson has operated as a makeshift centre-forward in Ueda's absence and could continue in that position if the latter fails to recover in time, although veteran striker Olivier Giroud also provides an alternative.

Meanwhile, Lyon will be without Tyler Morton, who recently underwent surgery for an abductor problem, while Pavel Sulc is recovering from a meniscus injury and Mohamed Ouedraogo is sidelined for the remainder of the campaign after rupturing his cruciate ligament.

Lois Openda also remains unavailable as he recovers from a fractured fibula, although the forward is expected to return in the coming weeks, while Steeve Kango could be available after rejoining group training following a period under concussion protocol.

Lille possible starting lineup:.

Ozer; Ngoy, Nianzou, Alexsandro, Perraud; Bentaleb, Andre, Mukau; E Mbappe, Haraldsson, Diaoune.

Greif; Athekame, Niakhate, Bacher, A Vinicius; Tessmann, Bidstrup, Tolisso; Nuamah, Merah, Nakamura.

Lyon's recent dominance in this fixture makes the visitors difficult to dismiss, particularly with Vicens hoping to make an immediate impression in his first match at the helm.

However, Lille's superior defensive record, unbeaten home form and greater consistency in the league should give Ancelotti's side the edge, and we expect the hosts to secure a narrow victory.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Saudi Arabia PIF led takeover came with PSR headroom from the Mike Ashley years and looser rules on owner-linked sponsorship.
  • Around £450m went on transfers in the Amanda Staveley era, but it was spent steadily, not decisively, and commercial income never grew fast enough to fund the next step.
  • By June 2024 Yankuba Minteh and Elliot Anderson had to go for a combined £60m-plus just to stay inside PSR.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Saudi Arabia PIF led takeover came with PSR headroom from the Mike Ashley years and looser rules on owner-linked sponsorship.

Around £450m went on transfers in the Amanda Staveley era, but it was spent steadily, not decisively, and commercial income never grew fast enough to fund the next step.

By June 2024 Yankuba Minteh and Elliot Anderson had to go for a combined £60m-plus just to stay inside PSR.

The structure never worked. Amanda Staveley was bought out in July 2024. Dan Ashworth left for Manchester United.

It has been revealed that paul Mitchell lasted under a year, branded the transfer operation “not fit for purpose” and ended up in a turf war with Eddie Howe which was largely irrelevant as every financial decision was made by Saudi Arabia PIF. Mitchell might have identified the problem but he had no answers.

Recent findings suggest that darren Eales and Dan Ashworth struggled to get past PIF’s processes. Good football people kept failing inside this framework. At some point you have to blame the framework.

Recent findings suggest that I agree Eddie Howe came back much too early and fatigued mentally and physically. But he still delivered the Champions League football.

It has been revealed that last seasons 12th with 17 league defeats was a bitter pill swallow and faced with the latest strategy and sale of his best players he walked away in July. He certainly was not at his best and was working with a divided squad where both Gordon and Tonali indicated to the club they were leaving before Christmas.

The central concern is our senior players simply had much higher earning potential at the six clubs who do not face the same SCR restrictions. Alexander Isak was reportedly assured of an improved deal by Amanda Staveley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi in March 2024. Paul Mitchell shelved it and Eddie Howe publicly cited PSR as the reason. Isak downed tools. Every dressing room and every agent drew the same conclusion: PSR then, SCR now, this club can’t pay you what you’re worth. So Gordon, Tonali and Bruno followed him out, with Trippier also gone.

Blaming Eddie Howe for transfers is a simplistic and nuanced view. None of the players signed in summer 2025 were his first choice, the embarrassing prolonged struggle to get transfers over the line are a clear manifestation of that. Nick Woltemade and Yoane Wissa were signed two weeks after the season started in desperation. That after the board took direct control of the Alexander Isak situation and prevented Eddie Howe from communicating with the player.

Industry observers note that beware the convenient narrative. It was Amanda Staveley’s naivety, then Paul Mitchell’s manner, then Alexander Isak’s greed, then Eddie Howe’s stubbornness. Now it is Matthias Jaissle’s tactics or Ross Wilson’s signings. A latest scapegoat every season is very useful to the people who never change. When the same problems outlast every individual blamed for them, the individuals were never the problem.

It has been revealed that under Ross Wilson the latest model has seen eight of the summer’s signings being 24 or younger, including 18-year-old Sean Steur from Ajax for about £20m. Dortmund is the stated template. Roughly £249m of players went out. The CEO’s line is that anyone under contract leaves “on our terms.”.

The problem is they still leave. Call it what it is: develop to sell. Under SCR, trading profit inflates the revenue side of the ratio, so I understand the logic.

According to recent reports, newcastle United are mid-table under Matthias Jaissle with the youngest squad in years. The question for Saudi Arabia PIF: is this a staging post at Newcastle United, or the destination?

Parker Tells West Ham Players An Uncomfortable Championship Truth

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (587 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Claretandhugh

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Ham United manager Scott Parker has identified defensive positioning, transitions and set pieces as areas he intends to improve following the international break.
  • West Ham are the Championship’s highest scorers, but their defensive record has repeatedly undermined their attacking performances.
  • According to recent reports, personally, I’ve always thought there were some relatively easy wins for Parker in terms of fixing West Ham’s defensive problems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham United manager Scott Parker has identified defensive positioning, transitions and set pieces as areas he intends to improve following the international break. Speaking to talkSPORT this morning, the Hammers boss explained why his team must become more disciplined without sacrificing their attacking ambition.

West Ham are the Championship’s highest scorers, but their defensive record has repeatedly undermined their attacking performances. Parker acknowledged that committing players forward can leave his side exposed, particularly when possession changes hands, and stressed the importance of what his players do behind the ball.

According to recent reports, personally, I’ve always thought there were some relatively easy wins for Parker in terms of fixing West Ham’s defensive problems. We’re scoring plenty of goals; we just need to sort the defence out. And if there’s one thing Parker has demonstrated during his managerial career, it’s that he knows how to organise a team defensively.

During his time at Burnley, Parker oversaw one of the most remarkable defensive campaigns in English football history.

His side conceded just 16 goals across 46 Championship matches during the 2024/25 season, setting a fresh record and keeping 30 clean sheets on their way to promotion.

Speaking in his talkSPORT interview, Parker discussed the importance of positioning when West Ham commit players forward, explaining that transitions and set pieces are particularly dangerous in the Championship.

And it’s interesting to hear him targeting transitions because that was exactly how West Ham conceded the opening goal against Blackburn Rovers in our last game.

Parker has informed West Ham players that they are now Championship players whether they like it or not.

But perhaps the most interesting part of Parker’s interview was his frank assessment of the mentality required from players who have dropped out of the Premier League.

He pointed out that the demands of the Championship are completely different, with players needing to accept the physical and psychological challenges of the division.

Parker then delivered a particularly pointed observation.

“If there’s a player here at this present moment in time playing in this division, it’s because that’s where he is.”.

It was a way of saying that irrespective of where you come from, it’s where you are that counts.

And no doubt there are players in the West Ham squad who consider themselves to be Premier League, European or international quality.

However, as of right now, they are Championship players, and Parker is quite right to point that out.

The latest gaffer has been promoted from this division three times, so I suspect he knows rather more about what is required than some of the players who have spent most of their careers in the Premier League.

Of course, the international break has given Parker a welcome opportunity to work with his players, although it’s important to remember that ten were away representing their countries.

Nevertheless, he will have learned considerably more about those who remained at Rush Green.

In particular, players such as full-backs Ezra Mayers and Joël Veltman have had the opportunity to work with the fresh manager, while a good number of West Ham’s midfielders have also remained at the club.

That should have allowed Parker to concentrate on some of the defensive positioning and tactical habits he discussed during the interview.

And let’s not forget that he’ll also have Thursday and Friday’s training sessions to work with his returning internationals ahead of Preston.

That is considerably more preparation time than he enjoyed before his opening two matches against Cardiff and Blackburn.

West Ham United’s Championship promotion hopes may have received an unexpected boost following confirmation that Swansea City manager Vítor Matos has left the Welsh club to take charge of French side Strasbourg.

The Portuguese coach had established Swansea as genuine promotion contenders, with the Swans sitting sixth in the Championship. His departure comes at an awkward time for a club attempting to maintain its challenge near the top of the table.

Sources indicate that strasbourg officially appointed Matos on Wednesday evening, replacing Hugo Oliveira. And whilst there’s no guarantee Swansea will suffer without him, I certainly regard this as good news for West Ham.

Matos was an extremely capable manager who had Swansea punching well above their weight.

When he arrived in November 2025, Swansea were languishing in 20th position. He eventually guided them to an 11th-place finish before establishing them amongst the promotion contenders this season.

The destination has turned out to be Strasbourg rather than Selhurst Park, but the potential consequences for Swansea remain much the same.

From a West Ham perspective, I’ll certainly take it.

Chelsea will be without five players for Saturday’s Premier League clash with Leeds United at Stamford Bridge.

Star striker Joao Pedro remains sidelined with a thigh injury and is joined in the treatment room by Jorrel Hato (back), Reece James (knee), Maxence Lacroix (hamstring) and Jamie Gittens (ankle).

However, Moises Caicedo (illness) and Josh Acheampong (unspecified) have recovered from minor complications. Acheampong could return to play alongside Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill in a back three, unless Xabi Alonso favours sticking with a four-man defence with Marco Palestra and Pep Chavarria as full-backs.

Jordan Henderson made the 700th appearance of his club career in the 1-0 defeat to his former side Sunderland a fortnight ago and he will hope to continue in centre-midfield role next to Caicedo and or Romeo Lavia.

Depending on Alonso’s formation, Pedro Neto could operate either out on the right flank or in a central attacking role next to Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer, while Estevao Willian is another attacking option pushing to start.

In a recent development, in the absence of Pedro, Danny Welbeck will hope to earn a place up front after netting a brace in Chelsea’s 6-3 EFL Cup win over Leeds in September. However, Alonso may prefer to use both Rogers and Palmer in central positions – Palmer also scored twice in that cup tie against Leeds while Rogers provided four second-half assists.

Martinez; Acheampong, Fofana, Colwill; Neto, Caicedo, Henderson, Palestra; Estevao, Rogers, Palmer.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that recent reports linking West Ham with Bristol City goalkeeper Joe Duncan are understandable.
  • But while Duncan is undoubtedly a talented young goalkeeper, West Ham must ask a simple question: why spend time, money and resources pursuing another developing keeper when they already have one of the country’s most highly-rated young goalkeepers sitting in their own academy?
  • Finlay Herrick joined the club at the age of six and has progressed through every level of the academy system.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that recent reports linking West Ham with Bristol City goalkeeper Joe Duncan are understandable. The 20-year-old has enjoyed an impressive loan spell at Southend United, earned a surprise senior Wales call-up and is attracting attention from a number of clubs.

But while Duncan is undoubtedly a talented young goalkeeper, West Ham must ask a simple question: why spend time, money and resources pursuing another developing keeper when they already have one of the country’s most highly-rated young goalkeepers sitting in their own academy?

Finlay Herrick joined the club at the age of six and has progressed through every level of the academy system. He was part of the famous side that won the FA Youth Cup and U18 Premier League South double in 2022/23, signed a long-term contract in 2024 and has represented England from U16 through to U20 level. Herrick, now aged 20, has already made three senior appearances for West Ham.

The standout moment came in the FA Cup quarter-final against Leeds United when he replaced Alphonse Areola in the 120th minute and immediately saved a penalty in the shootout. Although the Hammers ultimately lost, Herrick demonstrated the composure and personality required to perform under intense pressure.

He also acquitted himself well in the EFL second-round 4-1 win at Southampton back in August.

Sources indicate that in his last game, three saves, including a vital one-on-one against Fulham, were not enough as we were edged out of the EFL Cup 3-2 by our London rivals. However, our young custodian blamed himself for the third goal, saying he needed to be harsh on himself and should have done better to prevent it.

Industry observers note that regarding Duncan, he has come through Bristol City’s academy and gained valuable experience on loan at Tiverton Town and Farnborough before stepping up to National League football with Southend United. His performances have been good enough to earn a Wales senior squad call-up from Craig Bellamy despite never making a first-team appearance for Bristol City.

Southend manager Kieron Dyer and Bellamy have both spoken positively about his development, while West Ham are reportedly among several clubs monitoring his situation.

According to recent reports, one of the biggest criticisms supporters have of modern football is that clubs often look elsewhere rather than trusting their own youth products. You only have to look at former academy prospect Nathan Trott, who was regularly loaned out to other clubs and has now quickly established himself as the main keeper for Cardiff City.

Behind Herrick are a number of other keepers coming through the ranks, with high expectations of Lanre Awesu, who at just 18 years old has featured for the U21 side on a number of occasions. Standing at 6ft 5in, he has been highly praised by David Martin, along with fellow keeper Finley Hooper.

In a recent development, herrick has already spent 14 years at the club. He has excelled at youth level, earned England recognition, performed well on loan and shown promise when given an opportunity with the senior side.

At some point, development becomes about opportunity.

If a goalkeeper with Herrick’s pedigree cannot move up the pecking order, then what is the purpose of the academy pathway? What message does that give to Herrick, Awesu and Hooper?

With Hermansen failing to convince and Areola proving increasingly unreliable due to injuries, the moment for Herrick could arrive far quicker than anyone anticipated.

In my opinion, the Hammers should show faith in their own. The smartest signing West Ham can make may already be wearing number 49 at Rush Green!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham United have received a boost ahead of Saturday’s Championship clash with Preston North End, with striker Johnny Kenny ruled out through injury. The 22-year-old has suffered a hamstring tear and is expected to remain sidelined beyond Upcoming Year’s Day.

Sources indicate that preston manager Graham Alexander confirmed the extent of the injury in an interview with the Lancashire Evening Post, having lost Kenny during the defeat to Sheffield United earlier this month. The striker’s absence adds to Preston’s injury problems ahead of their visit to the London Stadium.

However, Preston have already demonstrated they can win without Kenny, having beaten Southampton in their previous fixture. Midfielder Léo Leroy is also available again after suspension, although captain Ali McCann remains sidelined.

Soungoutou Magassa was reinstated to the West Ham squad following the arrival of Parker.

Personally, I have a suspicion that Scott Parker will drop Mohamadou Kanté for this game and reinstate Soungoutou Magassa in midfield to protect his back four, irrespective of Preston’s attacking options.

Parker has already shown that he’s prepared to use Magassa, having recalled him for the Cardiff City match.

And with West Ham’s defensive problems continuing, I suspect the upcoming manager will want somebody sitting in front of the defence to provide additional protection.

It’s a possibility we’ve previously discussed when examining Parker’s plans for the international break, and the manager has now had considerably more time to work on his tactical approach.

Kenny’s absence is undoubtedly welcome news for West Ham, but it won’t dictate Parker’s team selection.

As recent training footage has demonstrated, Magassa has been involved in Parker’s preparations.

Whether that results in a starting place against Preston remains to be seen.

#61007. Liverpool vs Man United: Why England's biggest rivalry still matters amid United crisis

Liverpool vs Man United: Why England's biggest rivalry still matters amid United crisis

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1013 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 19 Nov 2026 16:09.
  • Liverpool and Manchester United will renew one of English football's fiercest rivalries at Anfield on Sunday, but rarely have the two clubs approached this fixture from such contrasting positions.
  • Liverpool sit fourth in the Premier League under Andoni Iraola, while United arrive in the relegation zone following a disastrous start to the 2026-27 campaign that cost Michael Carrick his job.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 19 Nov 2026 16:09.

Liverpool and Manchester United will renew one of English football's fiercest rivalries at Anfield on Sunday, but rarely have the two clubs approached this fixture from such contrasting positions.

Liverpool sit fourth in the Premier League under Andoni Iraola, while United arrive in the relegation zone following a disastrous start to the 2026-27 campaign that cost Michael Carrick his job.

According to recent reports, mauricio Pochettino's appointment has offered supporters renewed hope, although the Argentine could hardly have been handed a more demanding introduction. His first match in charge will be against the club United have historically regarded as their greatest rivals.

Recent findings suggest that the circumstances are extraordinary. United have collected just eight points from their opening 10 league matches, winning only once, and are already 10 points behind Sunday's opponents.

Yet the gulf in the table has done little to diminish the significance of the occasion.

In a recent development, for Liverpool and United supporters, this fixture has never depended entirely on league positions. Its importance comes from generations of competition for domestic supremacy, the history of two neighbouring cities and the enduring desire to establish which club holds the greater place in English football.

Debates about England's greatest football rivalry inevitably produce different answers.

Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur share one of the country's most intense local rivalries. Newcastle United and Sunderland have a derby rooted deeply in regional identity, while Manchester City and United have spent recent decades competing for the same major honours.

The historic tensions between Leeds United and Manchester United, or between Liverpool and Everton, are equally significant to the supporters involved.

Liverpool against United, however, occupies a distinctive position because it combines the prestige of two of England's most successful clubs with a rivalry between cities that predates professional football.

Liverpool developed into one of Britain's principal ports, while Manchester became an industrial powerhouse during the 19th century.

The opening of the Manchester Ship Canal in 1894 allowed goods to reach Manchester without passing through Liverpool's docks, becoming an enduring symbol of the economic competition between the two cities.

Football subsequently provided another arena for that rivalry.

Liverpool dominated English football during the 1970s and 1980s, winning league championships and European Cups while United struggled to match their domestic consistency.

The balance shifted dramatically under Sir Alex Ferguson.

United won 13 Premier League titles between 1993 and 2013, overtaking Liverpool's longstanding record of 18 English league championships in the process.

Ferguson's ambition to surpass Liverpool helped define United's most successful era, with the two clubs competing for supremacy even when they were not direct rivals for the title in a particular season.

Liverpool eventually ended their 30-year wait for a league championship under Jurgen Klopp in 2020 and drew level with United on 20 English top-flight titles by winning another in 2025.

That shared record has reinforced a rivalry measured across decades rather than individual seasons.

The head-to-head figures also demonstrate how closely contested the fixture has been historically.

Across 218 competitive meetings, United have recorded 85 victories to Liverpool's 72, with another 61 matches ending level.

However, those overall figures tell only part of the story.

Liverpool's extraordinary 7-0 victory at Anfield in March 2023 remains the largest winning margin in the fixture's history, while United demonstrated their ability to upset their rivals with a 3-2 victory at Old Trafford in May this year.

Results of that magnitude become part of the clubs' collective memories, ensuring that each new encounter carries the weight of previous triumphs and humiliations.

Sunday's meeting arrives at a particularly delicate moment for Manchester United.

The club's decision to replace Carrick with Pochettino reflects the scale of its problems, with a single Premier League victory leaving the Red Devils fighting to escape the bottom three.

The former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea manager officially began work on November 18, giving him only a few days to assess his squad before travelling to Merseyside.

As previously examined in Sports Mole's analysis of Pochettino's appointment and his preferred approach, the Argentine has built much of his reputation around pressing, collective organisation and developing young players.

Those principles will take time to establish, particularly in a squad that has struggled defensively throughout the campaign.

Anfield nevertheless provides an immediate opportunity to change the atmosphere surrounding the club.

A positive result would not erase United's difficult start, but taking points away from Liverpool could offer Pochettino an early foundation on which to build.

Defeat, particularly a heavy one, would bring another wave of scrutiny to a side already facing questions about its competitiveness.

Liverpool have their own reasons to attach considerable importance to the match.

Iraola, who replaced Klopp's successor Arne Slot in the summer, is preparing for his first competitive encounter with United as Liverpool manager.

His team remain in the Champions League positions, although their fourth-place standing leaves them with ambitions of closing the gap on the leaders.

Sunday therefore represents an notable test of Liverpool's progress under their new coach, as well as an opportunity to deepen their rivals' difficulties.

The stakes are different from those during the Ferguson era, when United regularly pursued championships, or the period when Liverpool were establishing themselves as Europe's dominant force.

But the nature of the rivalry means that United's current league position cannot make the match an ordinary fixture.

Both managers will experience this contest from their respective dugouts for the first time, while Pochettino faces the added challenge of beginning his United career in one of English football's most unforgiving away environments.

When Liverpool and Manchester United meet at Anfield on Sunday at 4.30pm, their immediate objectives will be markedly different.

In a recent development, for Liverpool, victory would strengthen their position near the top of the Premier League. For United, the occasion offers a chance to begin repairing a damaged season.

The rivalry itself has survived far greater changes in the fortunes of both clubs, and Sunday's encounter will be another reminder of why their meetings continue to command such attention.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A heated exchange at the London Assembly has thrust West Ham United’s London Stadium back into the spotlight, with Susan Hall challenging Mayor Sadiq Khan’s Chief of Staff, David Bellamy, over the stadium’s mounting losses and the failure to secure a naming rights sponsor.

The confrontation took place during the Assembly’s Budget and Performance Committee scrutiny, with Hall questioning why a venue of such prominence continues to cost taxpayers approximately £20 million annually, according to City AM’s report.

Bellamy insisted that City Hall remains in the market for a naming rights partner, with discussions ongoing. However, he acknowledged that West Ham’s relegation from the Premier League has made securing a lucrative sponsorship agreement more difficult.

Hall has accused the Mayor of failing to deliver a sponsorship deal despite having a decade to find one.

The exchange highlights the extraordinary financial problems surrounding the former Olympic Stadium and raises fresh questions about its long-term future.

According to recent reports, as Claret & Hugh previously reported, stadium officials have warned that naming rights may not be secured until at least 2028. We’ve also examined why even a £4 million sponsorship deal would do little to resolve the stadium’s wider financial problems.

In our latest Hammers Chat video, Geo and I discuss the confrontation, the stadium’s finances and whether a change of ownership could finally provide a solution.

Industry News: Tony Mowbray steps down as Blackburn Rovers manager with immediate effect due to health reasons - two years after bowel cancer battle forced him to leave Birmingham City

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (815 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 05:25 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 08:02 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers manager due to ill health.
  • The 62-year-old, who previously had to walk away from his job at Birmingham City in 2024 due to a battle with bowel cancer, leaves Blackburn with immediate effect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 05:25 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 08:02 EST, 17 November 2026.

Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers manager due to ill health.

The 62-year-old, who previously had to walk away from his job at Birmingham City in 2024 due to a battle with bowel cancer, leaves Blackburn with immediate effect.

The Championship side announced his departure with a statement from Mowbray. It read: 'Unfortunately, due to health problems, I have to step back from my role as Head Coach of Blackburn Rovers.

Recent findings suggest that 'I’m immensely proud of this group of players. Their dedication and professionalism have given us some memorable performances and wins, and I’ve loved working with them.

Sources indicate that 'Thank you to my coaching staff for all your hard work and for the support you’ve given me. It’s been a pleasure working alongside you.

'To the fans, thank you for the way you’ve supported me and the team this season. I’ve always tried to give you a team that you can be proud of. Your support has meant a great deal to me.

Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers boss due to ill health.

'I’m grateful to the Owners and Suhail (Pasha, chief operating officer) for giving me the opportunity to lead this great club once again.

Sources indicate that 'I’d ask that you give me and my family privacy at this time. Thank you for your understanding.'.

Mowbray leaves with Blackburn 13th in the Championship. He took over at the club in June this year having spent two years out of the game following his health complications at Birmingham City.

According to recent reports, the veteran manager suddenly stepped down as manager of Birmingham in February 2024 after undergoing surgery for bowel cancer. He had 15cm of his bowel removed during his treatment.

He took a temporary leave of absence after eight games in charge, before officially resigning from the role in May.

Mowbray, who has managed a host of English clubs, opened up publicly about his struggles, telling the Times that his children had feared the worst.

Sources indicate that 'I had the conversation with my family and you could see they were frightened,' he said. 'Was I frightened? My only thoughts were for my family, my three children and my wife and making sure they were OK.

Industry observers note that 'I had to put everything in order and I tried to. My wife saw our banking app for the first time in her life. It's little things like that. She understood. This was serious stuff. I felt she needed to know where we had our money, whether it was ISAs or pensions and what was in the bank.'.

According to recent reports, speaking on his diagnosis, which came after he collapsed when trying to answer the door, he added: 'My wife put me in the car and drove me back to hospital and they wanted to know why I was collapsing and in the condition I was,' he notes. 'They rehydrated me and put me on a drip overnight.

'I remember sitting there in bed and my kids' eyes were watering up. They were scared I wasn't going to live. How old were they? They were 15, 17 and 19. I could see the fear in their eyes.'.

Mowbray's comeback story when he was made Blackburn boss in the summer was one of the feel-good moments of the offseason. It has not been disclosed what his current health matter is.

Mowbray leaves Blackburn with the team in 13th place in the Championship table.

Blackburn Rovers owner Balaji Rao added his own statement, writing: 'Our thoughts are with Tony and his family as he steps back from his duties to focus on his health.

It has been revealed that 'Through our many meetings over the years, we’ve come to know Tony well and grown very fond of him. We’ve always admired his professionalism, his dedication and the passion he brings to his work at Blackburn Rovers.

After a humiliating defeat by Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. Alan Shearer has been asked to name his all time Newcastle United starting eleven.

The United and England legend accepting the challenge.

Not a bad Newcastle United starting eleven….

The Premier League record goalscorer talking to All Out Football and starting at the back.

Alan Shearer: “Shay Given in goal, Trippier on the right, I’m going to say Dan Burn because he scored in the final and helped us lift the trophy. I’m going to say Lewis Hall as a left-back and as the other centre-half I’m going to say, value for money it has to be Fabian Schar.”.

The former NUFC number 9 then moving on to midfield: “Rob Lee, Bruno…”.

Then finally Alan Shearer getting to the top of the pitch: “Beardsley without a doubt, Newcastle’s best ever player. Ginola, me and Les Ferdinand.”.

So that makes it this all time Newcastle United starting eleven, according to Alan Shearer:.

Shay Given Kieran Trippier Fabian Schar Dan Burn Lewis Hall Rob Lee Bruno Guimaraes Peter Beardsley David Ginola Les Ferdinand Alan Shearer.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Facing a sceptical fanbase, Didier Digard will be eager to win over the doubters at the first time of asking when Lens host Toulouse at the Stade Bollaert-Delelis on Saturday evening.
  • The two sides are level on 13 points from their opening 10 matches, with Les Sang et Or 11th in the Ligue 1 table and Les Violets one place below only on goal difference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 19 Nov 2026 16:21, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 16:25.

Facing a sceptical fanbase, Didier Digard will be eager to win over the doubters at the first time of asking when Lens host Toulouse at the Stade Bollaert-Delelis on Saturday evening.

The two sides are level on 13 points from their opening 10 matches, with Les Sang et Or 11th in the Ligue 1 table and Les Violets one place below only on goal difference.

Having got it wrong with Yannick Cahuzac, who lasted barely two months after succeeding the sacked Dino Toppmöller, it comes as little surprise that the Lens faithful have given Digard’s appointment a lukewarm reception, particularly given how his last managerial job ended.

Digard arrives fresh from his dismissal by bottom-of-the-table Le Havre, who failed to win any of their opening nine league matches of the 2025-26 campaign under his stewardship, and he now faces the task of arresting Les Sang et Or’s alarming slump.

Lens have lost five of their last seven matches in all competitions, including each of the last three, with a humiliating 9-1 home thrashing by Como in the Champions League sandwiched between league defeats to Lille (1-0) and Marseille (2-1) before the international break.

Le Sang et Or’s  current plight stands in stark contrast to last season, when they finished runners-up under Pierre Sage, who also guided the club to a first-ever Coupe de France triumph in May, so the latest man has a tough act to follow if he is to win the supporters over.

Sitting four points adrift of the European places and five clear of the relegation zone, Digard knows just how much Saturday’s result could matter, and shoring up a defence that has conceded 15 goals without keeping a single clean sheet in their opening 10 league fixtures will be high on his list of priorities.

While their tally of 17 goals at the other end is a respectable return, Lens have been no more than steady in front of their own supporters this season, winning three of their five league matches at the Stade Bollaert-Delelis and losing the other two, most recently that defeat to Marseille.

Toulouse, meanwhile, head to northern France in considerably better shape, having lost just one of their last seven league matches (W3, D3), with that solitary defeat coming away to Marseille on matchday nine.

Jens Berthel Askou’s side responded to that setback in emphatic fashion, beating Strasbourg 3-1 at home just before the international break, with Santiago Hidalgo and Mark McKenzie among the scorers and Giovanni Reyna netting a consolation for the visitors.

That result continued an intriguing pattern for Les Violets, whose three league wins this season (D4, L3) have all come in games in which they scored exactly three times, suggesting another free-flowing attacking display could be the key to taking maximum points from Lens.

However, Toulouse have won just one of their five away matches this season (D3, L1), conceding exactly twice in four of them, with their only clean sheet on the road coming in a 3-0 victory at Le Mans on October 16.

The visitors also have a poor head-to-head record to overcome, having won just one of their last 11 meetings with Lens in all competitions, although that solitary success did come at the Stade Bollaert-Delelis, a 1-0 win in January 2025.

Lens remain without Maik Nawrocki, Odsonne Edouard and Ismaelo Ganiou, with the trio sidelined by cruciate ligament, groin and knee injuries, respectively.

Andrija Bulatovic picked up a neck problem on international duty with Montenegro and is a slight doubt for Saturday, while Abdallah Sima remains sidelined with a thigh injury.

Jhoanner Chavez is also ruled out with a hamstring issue, but Franjo Ivanovic has recovered from a concussion and is available for selection.

Florian Thauvin has scored five goals and provided seven assists in Ligue 1 this season, meaning he has had a direct hand in more than 70% of his side’s league goals, and he will once again be the man to watch.

As for Toulouse, they will be without Rafik Messali, who is not expected back until December because of a muscle injury, while Thomas Jorgensen is a doubt after withdrawing from Denmark Under-21 duty with an undisclosed problem.

Aron Donnum is available again after serving a one-match suspension, and Mathis Amougou is also eligible after missing the Strasbourg game because of a clause in his loan agreement.

Casper Tengstedt leads the way for Toulouse with five league goals, although the forward has now gone three matches without scoring and will be eager to rediscover his touch in front of goal.

Risser; Baidoo, Gradit, Todibo; Abdulhamid, Titraoui, Haidara, Udol; Thauvin, Sotoca; Ivanovic.

Toulouse possible starting lineup:.

Restes; Diallo, Nicolaisen, McKenzie, Tape; Donnum, Casseres, Sigur; Jorgensen; Tengstedt, Hidalgo.

Lens have enjoyed plenty of success against Toulouse in recent meetings, and Digard’s arrival could give the hosts the lift they need to respond after a difficult spell.

However, their defensive frailties remain a major concern, and the visitors’ resilience on the road suggests they have more than enough about them to take something from this fixture.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Ham United v Preston North End EFL Championship London Stadium Saturday 21 November 2026, 3pm GMT.
  • Scott Parker’s first home match as West Ham United head coach is massively notable.
  • West Ham have collected one point from Parker’s opening two games and must start closing the gap to the automatic-promotion places.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham United v Preston North End EFL Championship London Stadium Saturday 21 November 2026, 3pm GMT.

Scott Parker’s first home match as West Ham United head coach is massively notable. Preston North End are bottom of the Championship and, while Saturday’s fixture is not mathematically must-win, realistically it feels very close to it.

West Ham have collected one point from Parker’s opening two games and must start closing the gap to the automatic-promotion places. After two uninterrupted weeks with much of his squad, this is the first proper opportunity to judge whether the new head coach has begun improving the organisation and intensity of the team.

It has been revealed that there is also the troubling matter of West Ham’s home form. I worried before relegation that the vast gaps between the London Stadium crowd and the pitch might turn it into a disadvantage rather than an advantage, and we now desperately need to begin winning there consistently.

Sources indicate that the London Stadium has not remotely resembled a fortress this season. Opponents have arrived believing they can frustrate West Ham, exploit the anxiety around the ground and capitalise when the players become nervous.

According to recent reports, as one former Championship striker recently observed, visiting teams have been enjoying the London Stadium experience. That situation has to change if West Ham are serious about challenging for automatic promotion.

Recent findings suggest that parker needs his players to begin promptly and give the crowd something to respond to. The longer this remains goalless, the more Preston will believe their long-ball approach and deep defensive shape can earn them something.

Scott Parker will need to make the London Stadium feel like home.

West Ham will dominate possession, so the challenge will be using it properly. Passing sideways in front of an organised defence will achieve very little; we need quicker movement, runners beyond the striker and enough tempo to pull Preston out of position.

Recent findings suggest that I expect West Ham to be considerably tighter defensively following Parker’s first extended spell on the training pitch. However, the international break has not been quite as useful as it initially appeared because several important players were away representing their countries.

Konstantinos Mavropanos was among those absent, while Max Kilman is suspended after reaching the disciplinary threshold at Blackburn. Parker has therefore been unable to work throughout the fortnight with the central-defensive partnership he will need on Saturday.

It has been revealed that I suspect Morato will move into his natural centre-back position alongside Mavropanos. That is probably the safe and predictable selection, although I would prefer to see Airidas Golambeckis given the opportunity.

The teenager has generally impressed when called upon and deserves serious consideration. As our examination of Parker’s defensive conundrum against Preston highlighted, the decision appears to be between Morato’s experience and Golambeckis’ encouraging performances.

Joël Veltman should start at right-back, while Ezra Mayers deserves to retain his place on the left. Kyle Walker-Peters continues to be assessed, but Parker has two natural and capable full-back options without needing to rush him back.

The biggest selection question surrounds the goalkeeper. I am finding Parker’s team difficult to predict primarily because I do not know whether he will retain Mads Hermansen or turn to Alphonse Areola.

Recent findings suggest that hermansen has produced an inconsistent sequence of performances. He excelled for Denmark against Portugal before making another clanger during the defeat by Norway, which will not have made Parker’s decision any easier.

Industry observers note that there has been considerable pressure for West Ham to make a change in goal, but Areola’s own fitness has reportedly been an issue. Until Parker confirms otherwise, my best guess is that Hermansen will retain his place.

I suspect Parker will stick with Hermansen.

Industry observers note that this is an ideal fixture in which to rebuild the goalkeeper’s confidence, but Preston’s likely use of long balls and set pieces means he must command his penalty area properly. Another nervous display would only intensify the debate but my own choice would be to select Finn Herrick.

Sources indicate that I expect Parker to continue with the 4-2-3-1 formation. Arne Engels and Soungoutou Magassa should form the central-midfield partnership, with Divine Mukasa operating further forward.

Magassa gives West Ham a recognised holding midfielder and should help protect a changed defence. That will allow Engels to move the ball forward and support Mukasa rather than both central midfielders occupying similar positions.

Preston’s victory over Southampton was built around an aggressive pressing approach, something Parker will have worked on during the break. I previously argued that West Ham must learn to play through Preston’s press, and this midfield should contain enough composure and energy to do it.

Sources indicate that jarrod Bowen will naturally start on the right, with Edvin Austbø on the left. In my opinion, Austbø has moved ahead of Manor Solomon in the pecking order and deserves a proper run in the team.

Joël Piroe should lead the attack. Parker needs to give West Ham’s most proven Championship goalscorer an extended opportunity rather than continually rotating strikers who have struggled to find any rhythm.

In a recent development, I expect five players who were away on international duty—Hermansen, Mavropanos, Mukasa, Austbø and Piroe—to start. The key defensive change should see Morato move inside to replace the suspended Kilman.

According to recent reports, preston earned their first victory under Graham Alexander by beating Southampton before the international break, so they should arrive with renewed confidence. However, both of their Championship wins this season have come at home.

Recent findings suggest that their away record is dreadful. Preston are winless on the road, having drawn once and lost six of their seven away league matches, including some heavy defeats.

Industry observers note that I expect them to use plenty of long balls, remain compact and try to frustrate West Ham. Even so, the Hammers have far better players and will enjoy the lion’s share of possession.

Quite frankly, it is time they showed the difference in quality. If West Ham cannot beat the Championship’s bottom club at home after Parker has been given two weeks to prepare, serious questions will remain about our promotion credentials.

Sources indicate that preston may make the opening stages awkward, but West Ham should eventually have far too much attacking quality. Parker’s team need to play with intensity, move the ball quickly and turn possession into genuine chances rather than merely dominating the statistics.

In a recent development, I expect a much more organised performance following the international break. Preston’s direct approach may still produce a goal, particularly with West Ham fielding a changed central defence, but this should be the afternoon Parker claims his first victory.

Prediction: West Ham United 4-1 Preston North End.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham United midfielder Arne Engels is attracting interest from Bundesliga side VfB Stuttgart, although the German club could struggle to afford the £22m summer signing.

Sources indicate that according to German newspaper BILD, as reported by Sport Witness, Stuttgart have identified Engels as one of several potential replacements for Angelo Stiller, who could leave the club next summer. Southampton’s Caspar Jander and Middlesbrough’s Aidan Morris are also under consideration.

Industry observers note that however, Stuttgart reportedly regard the cost of signing Engels as unrealistic, with West Ham unlikely to accept a substantial loss on a player who only arrived from Celtic in August. The German club previously wanted the Belgian during his time at Augsburg, so this is not an entirely newly introduced interest.

Look, clearly Engels is somebody that West Ham head of recruitment Nils Koppen values extremely highly.

As we reported when the £22m agreement with Celtic was reached, the Belgian had been Koppen’s primary midfield target throughout much of the summer. West Ham pursued him for weeks before finally getting their man.

I thought very swiftly he’d become one of the first names on the team sheet under Nuno Espírito Santo, and I suspect that will continue under Scott Parker.

So clearly he is a player who is admired.

That said, I’m not surprised Stuttgart are struggling to find value at £22m because I do think West Ham overpaid when we bought him from Celtic.

West Ham midfielders will play with more freedom under Parker which could unlock Engels value.

In a recent development, now, that price becomes fully justified if he helps get the team promoted this season. If not, then I’d have to say that so far he’s done little to justify the price tag.

It has been revealed that that’s not to suggest Engels is a bad player. He’s a busy, high-energy midfielder who covers plenty of ground and contributes to the team’s overall play.

But there’s a difference between being a good Championship midfielder and looking like a £22m player.

Indeed, when I recently assessed Koppen’s summer recruitment, Engels was one of the players I felt remained something of an unknown quantity in terms of value for money.

But, and here’s the important thing, West Ham manager Scott Parker has a habit of getting central midfielders scoring goals.

And if he can get Engels further up the pitch than Nuno Espírito Santo managed to, and into goalscoring positions, I suspect his value will rise if he becomes a goalscorer rather than just a busy, high-energy midfield player.

We’ve already had a glimpse of what might be possible.

Engels scored his first West Ham goal during the extraordinary 3-3 draw at Cardiff City in Parker’s opening match, as the Hammers recovered from three goals down at half-time.

That was one of the positives from a remarkable second-half performance, which I discussed in my player ratings following the Cardiff comeback.

However, against Blackburn, Parker used Engels in a deeper midfield role, with Mohamadou Kanté and Divine Mukasa operating further forward. As our Blackburn match report highlighted, that arrangement helped protect the defence but offered Engels fewer opportunities to get forward.

It will be interesting to see whether Parker can find a balance between the two.

Engels has the energy to get around the pitch, and if he can add regular goals to his game, the argument over whether West Ham paid too much could begin to look very different.

For now, Stuttgart’s interest looks more like an indication of Engels’ standing in the game than an immediate threat to West Ham.

The Belgian is under contract until 2031, with the club holding an option for another year, as confirmed by West Ham’s official website.

And with the Hammers attempting to win promotion at the first attempt, I can’t imagine Koppen being particularly enthusiastic about losing the player he worked so hard to sign.

Personally, I still believe £22m was too much money for what Engels has shown us so far.

But if Parker can turn him into a midfielder who regularly arrives in the penalty area and contributes goals, that assessment could change considerably.

And if those goals help West Ham get promoted, nobody will be complaining about the transfer fee.

Portsmouth will head on their travels for Saturday's Championship clash against Bolton Wanderers at the Toughsheet Community Stadium.

Pompey are currently sitting in 11th spot in the Championship standings, while the Trotters start the weekend in 18th position.

After winning promotion via the League One playoffs last term, Bolton's main priority is to secure survival in their first Championship campaign since 2018-19.

The Trotters right now enjoy a seven-point buffer to the bottom three after recording five wins, two draws and eight defeats in their 15 league games this season.

However, Bolton boss Steven Schumacher will be concerned by the fact his team have lost three of their last four matches, conceding at least three goals in each of those losses.

The most recent of those losses took place in their final outing before the international break against a Derby County side that had gone 10 games without a win.

Ruben Rodrigues's second Championship goal of the season gave Bolton a slender half-time lead at Pride Park, but the Trotters had no response as they conceded three second-half goals as their four-game unbeaten away run came to a disappointing end.

Bolton return to the Toughsheet Community Stadium for their first game back from the international break, and while they have lost their last three home matches, they can at least take inspiration from the fact they have avoided defeat in each of their last 14 second-tier encounters against Portsmouth (W9, D5).

Portsmouth, meanwhile, are just two points adrift of the top eight after winning six, drawing four and losing five of their 15 league games this term.

John Mousinho's side put themselves in playoff contention with a six-game unbeaten run (W4, D2), which included three consecutive home victories.

However, both of those impressive runs were ended by a narrow 2-1 defeat to promotion-chasing Stoke City before the international break.

Tyrese Shade put Pompey in front with his first goal for the club, but a goalkeeping error allowed Jack McGlynn to equalise, before Ben Wilmot netted a 77th-minute winner to condemn Portsmouth to their first home defeat since the start of September.

Their hopes of returning to winning ways on Saturday may be tempered by the fact they have won just one of their last six away games (D3, L2), although they have at least avoided defeat in each of their previous three road trips (W1, D2).

The visitors have failed to win any of their last four competitive away meetings with Bolton since Christian Burgess scored the decisive goal in a League One clash in January 2020.

Samuel Iling Junior is an option to start if Schumacher decides to make an alteration to the attacking trio behind forward Sam Dalby.

As for Pompey, their injury list features Benjamin Arthur, Connor Ogilvie, Mark Kosznovszky, John Swift, Keshi Anderson, Luke Brooke-Smith, Marko Milovanovic and Colby Bishop.

Ebou Adams will serve a one-match ban after picking up his fifth yellow card of the season in the defeat to Stoke City.

West Ham United manager Scott Parker has admitted that Alphonse Areola is unlikely to be available for Saturday’s Championship clash with Preston North End, leaving the Hammers with a familiar goalkeeping dilemma.

Speaking during his pre-match press conference, Parker explained that the club had attempted to push the Frenchman’s recovery but were struggling to get him ready.

“We tried to push it a bit, but it looks a little bit unlikely and we’ll leave it as long as we can before making a decision,” said the West Ham boss.

It has been revealed that this isn’t particularly surprising. It’s something we’ve discussed previously on Claret & Hugh, with concerns surrounding Areola’s match fitness and reports that he has been carrying too much weight.

And considering Parker has worked with the Frenchman before, one has to assume he’d be really keen to play him.

The fact that he isn’t selecting Areola suggests the goalkeeper simply isn’t ready for action, particularly following his recent injury setback.

Personally, my choice would be to give young Fin Herrick a chance.

I was speaking to my Hammers Chat counterpart Geo during our West Ham v Preston preview this week, and he made an excellent observation.

The one thing Mads Hermansen has consistently been good at is his distribution with the ball at his feet.

Unfortunately, his clanger for Denmark in their last game means even that aspect of his performances is now under scrutiny.

He’s got the yips: West Ham goalkeeper Mads Hermansen, whose recent performances have raised concerns about his confidence.

I actually think the best thing we could possibly do for Hermansen would be to give him a rest.

His confidence has clearly taken a battering, and his latest international mistake has only increased the pressure.

Let’s be fair, young Herrick can’t perform any worse than the Danish keeper has in the last few games.

And as our recent coverage of supporters’ goalkeeping preferences demonstrated, there is already considerable dissatisfaction with the current situation.

I appreciate throwing a youngster into such an important game carries risks, but there comes a point when continuing with an out-of-form goalkeeper becomes an equally significant gamble.

For me, Saturday presents an opportunity to try something different.

FC Utrecht and Cambuur will both be looking to return to winning ways when they meet at Stadion Galgenwaard on Saturday.

This weekend marks the first league meeting between the sides since May 2023, with their last two encounters both coming in friendly matches.

Back in the top flight after a three-year absence, Cambuur needed time to find their feet, losing each of their opening four matches before responding with an eight-game unbeaten run in all competitions - winning five and drawing three.

Nonetheless, overcoming reigning champions PSV Eindhoven was always going to be a tall order for Johan Plat’s side, who found themselves 3-0 down inside the opening 19 minutes and ultimately fell 5-2 at Kooi Stadion on November 8.

Sources indicate that while survival is expected to remain the Yellow-Blues’ primary objective, their recent purple patch suggests a push for continental football may not be entirely out of reach. Matches like this weekend’s will go a long way toward gauging their readiness for such ambitions.

It has been revealed that plat was beaten by his opposite number in their only previous meeting earlier this year. The 39-year-old now seeks to exact revenge and extend his side’s away unbeaten run to five matches, the last three of which have ended in victory.

Just under half of Cambuur’s 25 goals have come before half-time, and facing a team that has been outscored 15-4 in that period this season offers the visitors a significant opportunity to seize control of proceedings in the opening 45 minutes.

According to recent reports, after winning three of four matches following the September international break, Utrecht appeared to have turned a corner. However, back-to-back defeats against Telstar and, most recently, NEC suggest the ghosts of their struggles have not been fully exorcised.

Anthony Correia’s side have collected seven fewer points than at this stage last season - the biggest drop-off among all ever-present teams over that period - and early-season hopes of a continental finish have been significantly tempered.

In a recent development, with just a third of the campaign played, Utrecht currently sit 14th in the standings, only two points clear of the drop zone. A defeat this weekend could see them fall into the bottom three and potentially as low as 19th, depending on other results.

De Domstedelingen’s next three matches are against newly-promoted sides in the league and a second-division opponent in the cup. They will be eager to string together a positive run and relieve some of the pressure on Correia before their first December Eredivisie fixture against Ajax.

Only Saturday’s opponents have scored more goals than Utrecht’s 21 among bottom-half sides, but the Cupfighters have struggled defensively, conceding 34 goals to leave them with the division’s second-leakiest defence behind bottom club Willem II.

FC Utrecht form (all competitions):.

Cambuur form (all competitions):.

Miliano Jonathans and Noah Ohio remain sidelined with ACL injuries, and neither is expected to return before next year.

Victor Jensen and Kevin Paredes are unavailable for the hosts due to knee injuries, while Alonzo Engwanda (hamstring) has not featured since May.

With five goals in nine league matches, Artem Stepanov has already matched his tally from last season, but the 19-year-old has failed to score in each of his last five outings.

Jamal Amofa is unlikely to feature again this season after suffering an ACL injury in October, making him one of three Dutch absentees for Cambuur alongside Daan Visser and Damian Westerhof.

Wout Asselman is nearing a return to action, although the Belgium international remains a major doubt for this weekend.

FC Utrecht possible starting lineup:.

Barkas; Vesterlund, Didden, Panagiotou, Kloosterboer; Broholm, Overeem, De Wit; Alarcon, Stepanov, Cathline.

Cambuur possible starting lineup:.

Jansen; Costarelli, Van Duijl, Baouf, Boauh; Hamache, Souren, Maertens, Ceka; Vink, Binder.

Cambuur are winless in regulation time across their last six visits to Utrecht and have struggled historically on the road against this weekend’s opponents.

Given Utrecht’s defensive frailties, a clean sheet for the hosts appears unlikely, but we expect them to do enough to secure all three points.

West Ham United manager Scott Parker has spoken positively about Joël Piroe ahead of Saturday’s Championship clash with Preston North End, raising an interesting question over his starting striker.

During his pre-match press conference, Parker acknowledged the Dutchman’s impressive goalscoring record and revealed that he was looking forward to spending more time working with him.

According to recent reports, “I’ve known about Joël, having played against his teams. His goalscoring record is really good,” said Parker.

“It’s a shame for us he’s been away, but he’s in good form, and I’m looking forward to working with him more.”.

Personally, I would 100% start Piroe ahead of Taty Castellanos, irrespective of how well the Argentine might have trained during the international break.

Piroe is a proven Championship goalscorer, and Parker knows all about him from his previous experience managing in this division.

I think he very much deserves a run of games in an attempt to fire at least one of our strikers into action.

The alternative is to continue persevering with Castellanos, who has been a considerable disappointment since West Ham’s relegation.

And there is another factor to consider.

As Claret & Hugh exclusively revealed, the club are exploring the possibility of selling Castellanos in January, with Nils Koppen already investigating potential replacements.

Further reports from Argentina have suggested the striker wants to leave, although no departure has been agreed.

Piroe is admired by Scott Parker.

I don’t think there’s any mystery surrounding what Piroe offers.

He knows the Championship, he knows how to score goals in it, and he’s already demonstrated that he can contribute to this West Ham team.

As we’ve previously argued when discussing Parker’s selection options, Piroe has a compelling case to start ahead of Castellanos.

Of course, the manager will have his own ideas about how he wants his centre-forward to play.

But given the lack of goals from our recognised strikers, I’d rather see Parker give the Dutchman a proper opportunity than continue waiting for Castellanos to discover some form.

For me, Piroe starts against Preston.

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 04:43 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 09:33 EST, 17 November 2026.

Premier League presenter Ellie Collins issued a warning to her followers after learning that she had been being impersonated on social media.

The 26-year-old has over 58,000 followers on Instagram having built up a loyal fanbase via her work on broadcasters covering the top flight and NFL in the US.

But Collins was forced to make a statement after an imposter was found to have been reaching out to people in her name over a number of months.

'I want to make people aware that someone has been impersonating me on WhatsApp, messaging high-profile athletes, pretending to be me with their username set to my name and a picture of me,' she told her followers on the social media app.

'This has been happening on and off for several months and seems to be upping in frequency more recently.

'I have reported this to the police and they’ve asked that I share it on here to make people aware, particularly anyone I have worked with or connected with in the football/sports world.

Premier League presenter Ellie Collins has warned fans of an impersonator pretending to be her on social media (All photos source: Instagram/Ellie Collins).

The 26-year-old maintains an active presence on the site and has over 58,000 followers.

After previously working as a waitress, Collins transitioned into broadcasting four years ago.

Since starting her career in the media, Collins has had the opportunity to interview a number of sports stars including Frank Lampard.

'If you receive a message from someone claiming to be me... it’s most likely not. If you don’t have my personal number and are unsure, just DM me on Instagram.

'If you receive anything suspicious, please send it to me directly so I can keep a record of it.

'Thank youuu (purple heart emoji, winking emoji),' she signed off.

Collins has worked in the media since joining IMG Media as an assistant five years ago.

Since 2022, the former waitress has served as a presenter for Premier League productions, which has led to opportunities to interview sports stars including Andy Robertson, John Terry, Bruno Fernandes, Conor Gallagher and Cody Gakpo.

Collins has also worked a number of events beyond the domestic league, such as Wimbledon and the 2025 Champions League final.

This year, she also covered the Open for Sky Sports from Royal Birkdale, and racing at York's Ebor Festival with ITV.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Milan Futuro decided to go in a new direction this summer by appointing Sergio Navarro, but is it working so far?

Industry observers note that milan launched the Futuro project ahead of the 2024-25 season. with the aim of creating a pathway for academy players to break into the first team. The project was designed to bridge the physical and technical gap between the Primavera and senior football.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In a recent development, things didn’t go well in year one, as Daniele Bonera didn’t see out the season as the head coach. He recently stated he didn’t think the squad was ready for the level, and ultimately Massimo Oddo was unable to save the team from relegation to Serie D, the fourth tier of Italian football.

According to recent reports, with promotion back to Serie C the objective, this summer the Rossoneri turned to Sergio Navarro, a coach with good pedigree in Spain. The Futuro now appear to have a clearer structure, a defined playing identity and the right guidance, as Rohit Rajeev has outlined.

Under Barquero, Milan Futuro operate in a 4-2-3-1 formation. Asanji leads the line, with Ossola playing as the number 10 and Vos and Guernier occupying the wide positions.

Plazotta and Pandolfi form the double pivot, while Cisse and Pagliei partner at centre-back, with Perera and Colombo completing the back four.

In a recent development, milan Futuro favour a possession-oriented approach, circulating the ball patiently at a measured tempo while waiting for gaps to emerge in the opposition’s defensive structure. They also use passing triangles effectively to create short passing options and play through the opposition’s high press.

In possession, Milan Futuro adopt a 3-1-6 structure, with Barquero showing little hesitation in committing players forward to create numerical overloads in the opposition half.

Asanji positions himself just behind the opposition’s defensive line, keeping the centre-backs occupied and preventing them from stepping forward freely. Meanwhile, Pandolfi and Plazotta maintain parallel positions in the double pivot, providing a stable base for the attacking structure.

In the opposition half, Milan Futuro keep the distances between players very short, allowing them to combine through quick, one-touch passes.

In a recent development, this also helps them create ball-sided overloads, with two or three players surrounding the Milan player in possession to provide close passing options. Once they enter the opposition half, the tempo increases as Milan look to become more direct and progress towards goal.

Similar to Amorim’s approach at Sporting, Milan Futuro form vertical corridors with three players positioned one behind another. This structure facilitates quick passing combinations while also creating movement to manipulate the opposition.

When Milan players drop to form these corridors or create overloads, they often drag defenders with them, opening spaces elsewhere to exploit.

It has been revealed that milan Futuro look to press the opposition high up the pitch, adopting a 4-4-2 shape with a man-oriented pressing scheme. This allows them to put pressure on the opposition’s build-up and restrict the time and space available to play out from the back.

It has been revealed that milan Futuro also set up pressing traps by deliberately leaving the opposition’s wide player unmarked. The pass towards the wide player acts as the pressing trigger, prompting Milan’s players to jump out of their positions and aggressively close down the receiver, while cutting off the available passing options.

Milan Futuro maintain an extremely narrow defensive shape, prioritising the protection of central spaces and forcing the opposition towards the flanks.

Once the opposition attempts to progress through the wide areas, the press shifts across to create numerical overloads around the ball, while Guernier and Colombo provide cover and prevent the opposition from switching play to the opposite flank.

Perhaps the most important aspect of Barquero’s approach is his willingness to build the system around his players’ strengths and allow them the freedom to express themselves.

In a recent development, rather than focusing solely on tactical adaptability, he appears equally committed to their individual development and helping them grow as footballers. Here are a few examples.

One of Milan Futuro’s methods of chance creation is to play direct passes into Asanji. His ability to position himself between the ball and the opposition defender, using his physicality to shield possession and hold up play, is crucial to this approach.

Rather than asking him to adapt to the role of a more technically oriented, ball-playing striker, Barquero has built a mechanism that makes the most of his existing strengths.

Perhaps the clearest demonstration of Barquero’s coaching ability is his utilisation of Vos and Guernier. Guernier is a natural winger/forward, while Vos is more accustomed to playing as an attacking midfielder.

Within the 3-1-6 structure, Vos often inverts from the left flank into an inside-left role, allowing Perera to provide the width.

In a recent development, at times, he is also given the freedom to interchange positions with Plazotta, allowing him to drop into midfield or advance further up the pitch. This positional freedom helps him develop his midfield qualities and realise his potential.

Guernier, meanwhile, tends to maintain his width, stretching the opposition’s defensive line and creating space for Vos and the other attackers to exploit.

Barquero also gives Guernier the freedom to take on his direct opponent, even when he is outnumbered, allowing him to use his dribbling ability without being restricted by the team’s structure.

Ossola, who is particularly effective at receiving between the lines and turning with the ball, is allowed to operate higher up the pitch, closer to the opposition’s defensive line.

Idrissi, on the other hand, prefers to receive possession deeper, where he can dictate play with his passing range or carry the ball forward through dribbling.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mark Noble has provided an interesting insight into how West Ham United’s recruitment operation is working under Scott Parker, revealing that Nils Koppen is in regular contact with the coaching staff about the players the club needs.

Speaking in an interview with West Ham’s official website, Noble explained that the Director of Player Recruitment is arriving at Rush Green as early as 6.30am, watching training and discussing the squad with Parker and his coaches.

Industry observers note that with the January transfer window approaching and West Ham desperate to secure promotion, it’s encouraging to hear that recruitment discussions are taking place. But for me, the most important part of Noble’s revelation has very little to do with what time Koppen arrives for work.

Quite frankly, whether Koppen arrives at half six in the morning is neither here nor there.

Much of the analytical and recruitment work can be carried out perfectly well from wherever somebody can plug into the internet.

What I find far more crucial is the open dialogue Noble has described.

He explained that Koppen watches training and that the coaching staff speak openly with him about the players they believe West Ham need.

Koppen then works with the club’s scouts and analysts in the background, allowing Parker and Noble to concentrate on coaching.

That strikes me as a huge plus and potentially a massive step in the right direction.

It also appears to represent a departure from the way things have operated previously, when questions were regularly raised about whether recruitment decisions matched the manager’s requirements.

As we discussed following Parker’s talkSPORT interview, the manager is absolutely right to concentrate on improving the players already at his disposal rather than becoming consumed by January transfers.

But that only works if the recruitment department understands precisely what he needs.

We know from our recent dialogue with a club insider that Koppen has begun looking for another striker, and Noble’s comments suggest those discussions are taking place alongside the coaching staff’s assessment of the squad.

That’s exactly how it should work.

Ultimately, I’m far more interested in whether Koppen signs the right players than whether he’s the first person through the door at Rush Green.

But if the people coaching the team and those recruiting for it are finally speaking openly about what West Ham need, that has to be encouraging.
