📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails. Managers often envisage the worst outcome when the clock ticks down, and here, in the 93rd minute, Bournemouth had a corner.

According to recent reports, he needn’t have worried. As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points. It was a catch, too, that put the gloss on another impeccable personal afternoon.

Industry observers note that when Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient. This dour 1-0 success, though, proves he is taking them in the right direction: he is the first Liverpool manager since Joe Fagan in 1983 to start with five unbeaten league games.

Alexander Isak might have scored the goal that leaves Bournemouth winless in the Premier League but this success owed everything to Alisson’s enduring brilliance – a comment that also applies to Virgil van Dijk – the enormous promise of Jérémy Jacquet and the grit of Ronaldo Araújo.

You go to top level football matches hoping to see something that will take your breath away and how Alisson did that in the 17th minute with a reflex save from an Evanilson backheel, the shape of his body resembling a fielder in the slips diving to prevent a boundary.

It proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

Industry observers note that “It was a really good fight,” Alisson said, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”.

Any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

Since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

Sources indicate that “He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola said. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”.

In a recent development, don’t confuse positivity about one aspect of the team as being a guide to its collective health. There was always a chance this contest would become a cagey affair and, Evanilson’s chance aside, the opening 45 minutes were as flat as you could imagine.

Iraola again played his three £100m+ signings but Bradley Barcola is still adjusting to the physicality of English football and Florian Wirtz is still finding it difficult to impose himself on a game; patience with the German will not be infinite.

He would do worse than to look at Isak, who is now on a run of four goals in four league games and is influencing games in the manner Liverpool envisaged when they broke the British transfer record to sign him last August.

Sources indicate that isak had an unusual afternoon. His only shot in the first half almost took out some low-flying pigeons, a cross early in the second half was sliced so badly that the weekend hackers on the nearby Queens Park golf course would have felt a flood of sympathy but then he got his third opening.

Cody Gakpo, who could have been in Manchester City blue had the cards played out differently earlier this month, wriggled down the right flank and squeezed in a cross that Isak seized upon and turned in from six yards. Liverpool never looked back.

Industry observers note that alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4.

Industry observers note that “A striker’s job is like this,” Iraola stated, who badgered Isak persistently to press Bournemouth’s defence. “He had a couple of crosses that he did not hit properly or control. He has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition’s half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals.”.

In a recent development, one, ultimately, was enough to see off Bournemouth, whose start to the campaign is something of a riddle. They shouldn’t be anywhere near the relegation places but that is the reality and Thursday’s historic Europa League win in Real Sociedad couldn’t mask the home crowd’s frustration.

It has been revealed that “Our attitude and effort is good,” head coach Marco Rose said. “But, at this level, small things and little details decide games.”.

Speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Iraola stated: “I’m obviously happy with the result because I know this is a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points. And we could see it, especially in the beginning of the game. In the first 20 minutes we weren’t at the level [required] and it cost us. We finished the first half better and in the second half we played better, but that beginning of the game has surprised us, not surprised us [because] we knew where we were coming but it [was] difficult for us.”.

Industry observers note that jeremy Jacquet has made the kind of quietly authoritative start to his Liverpool career that showed why there was such excitement in February within the club when they completed his deal. So much focus on so many players but Jacquet has never been anything other 7.5/8 out of 10.

Speaking about the job the Dutchman is doing to fill the void left by Mohamed Salah on the right flank, Ashley Young said on Sky Sports: “Players have to step up when you lose substantial players and you get the opportunities. I think Cody Gakpo is doing that. He’s a bit fortunate [in the build-up to Liverpool’s goal] but you create your own luck. He gets the ball down the line, that’s what you want to do and he puts the ball in the box. That’s what Isak’s waiting for.”.

Andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

His first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

In a recent development, everything Iraola has said and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

There is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has noted that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he mentioned: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

“We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”.

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

Adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He remarked: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”.

Industry observers note that good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool and Bournemouth as Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium for the first time since his massive move up north. The Basque propelled Bournemouth to newly introduced heights, guiding the club into Europe and his successor, Marco Rose, ensured they made a winning start to life on the Continent by defeating Real Sociedad in midweek.

Previewing Iraola’s Vitality Stadium return, Craig Beazley, host and creator of the Up The Cherries In All Departments podcast, said: “We’ve now got the Andoni Iraola return … Andoni is very much a legend really, there should be a statue of Sir Eddie Howe and Sir Andoni Iraola [outside the ground] as well.”.

Across three seasons, Iraola guided Bournemouth to 12th, ninth and sixth in the Premier League, winning 47 of his 127 matches in charge (37 per cent).

Liverpool are still acclimatising to his exacting style of play and their results suggest as much. They are 10th in the table having drawn three and won one, impressing in flashes but struggling to maintain consistently productive final-third patterns and pressing structures. Deploying Ronald Araújo at right-back has proved effective, though, with Liverpool conceding just two goals in their last four matches.

The Cherries are searching for their first Premier League win of the season and have retained the 4-2-3-1 shape from the Iraola days, with Rose preferring a similarly vertical attacking strategy. They continue to leverage their strengths in transitions and in wide areas as Adrien Truffert rains in crosses for any one of Bournemouth’s exuberant frontline to pounce on.

Elsewhere, Manchester City welcome Sunderland, who also secured a Europa League win during the week, to the Etihad while in-form Leeds United host Crystal Palace knowing a win would lift them into the top four.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 19 Nov 2026 21:26.

Bournemouth boss Marco Rose has revealed Alex Scott will start at least one of the next three competitive matches.

Scott has not played for Bournemouth since September after sustaining a thigh injury in England’s 7-0 win over Croatia at the start of October.

The midfielder missed the next eight matches before he returned to the matchday squad for the 2-1 victory over Ipswich Town before the international window.

However, Rose opted against risking Scott at Portman Road, giving him the chance to build up his fitness over the two-week break.

Bournemouth will resume their campaign with a home meeting with Nottingham Forest on Saturday, before they head on their travels for games against Celta Vigo and Fulham in the Europa League and Premier League respectively.

Speaking ahead of Saturday’s fixture, Rose has confirmed that Scott will start at least one of the next three matches for the Cherries.

Sources indicate that "We have many games in the upcoming weeks. Next week we have three games, so there are a lot of choices.” Rose mentioned in Thursday’s pre-match press conference.

Recent findings suggest that “For sure, he is going to start one game in this. We have to increase the match time step by step.".

Forward Junior Kroupi missed the first two months of the season after undergoing foot surgery in the summer.

As a result, Rose was keen to exercise caution when Kroupi returned to action last month, handing him four substitute appearances before he linked up with Zinedine Zidane's France squad.

Kroupi made his international debut in the 3-1 defeat to Italy before he scored his first goal for France in Sunday's 2-1 win over Turkey.

While both of those appearances came from the bench, Rose has now provided an revision on whether Kroupi is in a position to start games.

"Junior is ready to get more match time and even to start," the Bournemouth boss said.

In regard to absentees, the Cherries are likely to be without Juanlu Sanchez, Julian Araujo and Alex Toth.

Mauricio Pochettino's record vs Liverpool: Can he overcome Reds litmus test on Man Utd managerial debut?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (824 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Saikat Mandal | 19 Nov 2026 21:29, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:08.
  • Mauricio Pochettino has taken the plunge into unfinished Premier League business, accepting the daunting challenge of taking charge of Manchester United at arguably the lowest ebb in their modern history.
  • Since Sir Alex Ferguson's departure, the Red Devils have endured a steady and, at times, bewildering decline, although few could have envisaged the club spiralling to such depths.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 19 Nov 2026 21:29, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:08.

Mauricio Pochettino has taken the plunge into unfinished Premier League business, accepting the daunting challenge of taking charge of Manchester United at arguably the lowest ebb in their modern history.

Since Sir Alex Ferguson's departure, the Red Devils have endured a steady and, at times, bewildering decline, although few could have envisaged the club spiralling to such depths.

Sitting in the bottom three of the Premier League table after 10 games, Man Utd find themselves navigating one of the darkest chapters of their history in more than two decades.

Michael Carrick had offered plenty of promise last season after steering the club back into the Champions League, but that resurgence proved painfully short-lived, with the momentum failing to carry into the latest campaign and the hierarchy eventually losing patience with the Englishman.

A total of 11 managers, including interim appointments, have come and gone since 2013, and while the Old Trafford hotseat retains its considerable allure, the red carpet awaiting its latest occupant has long since been replaced by a bed of nails.

By accepting the offer, Pochettino has willingly grasped the poisoned chalice, although he could yet emerge as the Red Devils' long-awaited Messiah if he is afforded the time and authority to mould the squad in his own image and build something capable of enduring.

A trip to Anfield represents the ultimate litmus test for any Manchester United manager, and Pochettino could hardly have been handed a more imposing introduction to life in the Old Trafford dugout.

The two most successful clubs in English football share a rivalry of extraordinary magnitude, one whose history, intensity and cultural significance are difficult to replicate anywhere else in Europe's major leagues.

Curiously, however, it has been a rarity for both sides to enjoy their periods of absolute dominance simultaneously, with the balance of power traditionally swinging one way before shifting back after a prolonged spell.

Liverpool ruled the roost throughout much of the 1970s and 1980s, before the Red Devils seized the mantle and established themselves as England's pre-eminent force over the following two decades.

That hierarchy has shifted once again, with Liverpool restoring their position among the country's leading powers and adding two more league titles to their illustrious collection.

Pochettino's immediate priority will be to drag Man Utd out of their current mire, but the longer-term ambition must surely extend beyond mere recovery: restoring the club's former stature and, ultimately, knocking Liverpool off their perch once again.

Across his managerial career, the 54-year-old has faced Liverpool 19 times, winning three, drawing five and suffering 11 defeats, a record that makes for sobering reading ahead of his latest meeting with the Reds.

One of those losses came on the grandest stage of all: the Champions League final, when Divock Origi struck the decisive goal to etch his name into Anfield folklore and condemn Pochettino's Tottenham Hotspur to defeat.

Curiously, however, some of the Argentine's most memorable moments against Liverpool came when he was managing Southampton.

Back in 2013, Pochettino, then still a relatively unheralded figure in English football, masterminded a tactical masterclass at Anfield, where Southampton suffocated Liverpool's attacking threat with an aggressive press executed with remarkable discipline and control.

The Saints emerged with a famous 1-0 victory, providing an early glimpse of Pochettino's tactical credentials before his subsequent move to north London.

His time at Tottenham, by contrast, proved considerably less fruitful against the Merseyside giants, with Pochettino managing just one victory in 13 meetings.

That solitary success came in emphatic fashion, as Spurs swept Liverpool aside 4-1 at Wembley Stadium during their temporary stay at the ground in the 2017-18 campaign, while he also oversaw a 1-1 draw against the Reds during his brief spell at Chelsea.

Few would blame Pochettino if Man Utd were to come away from Anfield empty-handed, particularly given the lack of time he has had to prepare his side for such a daunting assignment, while even a hard-fought draw would represent an excellent result.

Having arrived at Old Trafford at such a turbulent juncture, it would be unrealistic to expect the Argentine to weave his magic overnight, but the Red Devils arguably need him now more than he needs them, with the club crying out for direction, stability and a clearly defined footballing identity.

Through meticulous coaching, astute recruitment and, crucially, the unwavering backing of the hierarchy, Pochettino could gradually restore the foundations that have been missing for so long and give the Red Devils a genuine platform from which to rise again.

For now, though, the Argentine must resist the temptation to look too far ahead and simply embrace the challenge in front of him, because while the Anfield cauldron represents a formidable first examination, it also offers him an opportunity to make an early statement and begin a new chapter at Manchester United on his own terms.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:40 EST, 17 November 2026.

Sebastien Pocognoli insists he’s unconcerned about calls for his head after a dismal start to his time in charge of Scotland.

Monday’s 4-0 defeat to Switzerland confirmed that the Belgian’s side finished a distant third in their Nations League section with the only two wins in six games coming against North Macedonia.

After a decent start to the match in St Gallen, Scotland fell behind to a Lewis Ferguson own goal and the result was put beyond doubt when the Swiss scored two quick goals at the outset of the second half.

With another performance falling way short of expectations and little sign of progress, the newly introduced manager is increasingly coming under pressure.

Despite only being in charge for 13 weeks, pundits including Michael Stewart have already called on the Scottish Football Association to draw a line under Pocognoli’s reign.

Industry observers note that adamant that he’s not feeling the heat, though, the 39-year-old insisted: ‘I am not thinking about this. I am just looking ahead to the next camp in March and the start of the qualification.

Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli is confident he'll get Scotland back on track.

Skipper Andy Robertson reacts at full-time to the 4-0 defeat against Switzerland.

‘We have to take the most we can from the last two camps and try to build something strong for the next one. The objective is to reach the Euros in the best position possible.

Industry observers note that ‘We will have ups and downs and it was not good in terms of the score against Switzerland. But, for me as a coach, it was a good game to see us against a strong nation away from home. That’s something we have to take into the future.’.

Asked how he dealt with the growing clamour for his dismissal, he replied: ‘I don’t accept this to be honest. It’s always like this when you have a bad moment, when you think about the past. But always thinking about the past is an energy taker — we have to look forward.’.

The successor to Steve Clarke, Pocognoli has tried to bring in a more attacking philosophy via a 3-4-2-1 formation.

While his reluctance to adapt has also drawn widespread criticism, he claims he’s not averse to coming up with a different approach.

Sources indicate that ‘It’s possible,’ he added. ‘I did it in Monaco and we won many tough games with a back four. I also won many good games with a back three.

Sources indicate that ‘We played in the Champions League and in half of the games we played with a different shape, so it doesn’t mean that I’m not flexible. But the timeline is to do what we are trying to do now.’.

It has been revealed that asked if the job was proving to be tougher than he anticipated, Pocognoli mentioned: ‘No. I think we nearly had a good game. It was just the score and the aspects in the boxes. That’s where there’s disappointment.

‘It’s step by step. And we have created a lot of chances in four of the six games. And in these six games we played one of them with 10 men and another where we were not on the level at all against Slovenia.’.

By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 21:32.

Tottenham Hotspur are sweating over the availability of James Maddison ahead of Saturday's Premier League encounter with Ipswich Town, with question marks remaining over whether the attacking midfielder will be fit enough to feature.

Roberto De Zerbi is contending with a lengthy list of injury doubts, as Mykhaylo Mudryk, Martin Dubravka, Savio, Mathys Tel, Lucas Bergvall and Tosin Adarabioyo all face late assessments for various ankle, knee, muscle and calf problems, while Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert remain sidelined with knee problems.

With Dubravka doubtful, Antonin Kinsky is poised to retain the gloves between the sticks behind a four-man rearguard featuring Pedro Porro, Micky van de Ven, Andy Robertson and Jan Paul van Hecke.

Remarkably, no Spurs player has scored more league goals than Van Hecke this term, a notable statistic for the two-goal centre-back as the hosts prepare to welcome the Tractor Boys.

In the engine room, Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes are expected to form a central midfield partnership to dictate the tempo of the contest.

Further forward, Archie Gray could be deployed in an advanced central role if Maddison is not risked from the off, flanked by Mohammed Kudus and Omar Marmoush in a dynamic creative trio.

Although Kudus has yet to score a league goal this season, the playmaker's three assists and ability to threaten from unlikely positions make him a potential match-winner for the home side.

Leading the line will be Dominic Solanke, who will look to capitalise on that creative service and spearhead the North Londoners to maximum points on Saturday afternoon.

Tottenham Hotspur possible starting lineup:.

Kinsky; Porro, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Tonali, Fernandes; Kudus, Gray, Marmoush; Solanke.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 17:34 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:49 EST, 17 November 2026.

Chelsea star Pedro Neto lost his cool while playing for Portugal in their win over Wales as he received two yellow cards in as many minutes before clashing with opposing manager Craig Bellamy.

The Blues winger had in fact scored in the game, netting his side's second goal at the Cardiff City Stadium, but saw his game fall apart in the second-half.

He was first booked for a high challenge on the back of Brennan Johnson's leg – a tackle which some may argue could have been a red in itself.

One minute and 59 seconds later, he was shown his second yellow when he slid in on Johnson again. He didn't appear to make too much contact, if any, but left the Wales man sprawling to avoid it.

German referee Sven Jablonski highlighted no hesitation in sending Neto off, but the winger wasn't going to take it lying down.

He had to be held back by captain Bruno Fernandes as he tried to confront Johnson, and seemingly managed to shout in his direction before reluctantly making his way off the field.

Pedro Neto was sent off while playing for Portugal against Wales after two yellow cards in under two minutes.

He also had a confrontation with Wales manager Craig Bellamy (right) as he left the field of play.

Before that, though, he had a conversation with Wales boss Craig Bellamy, with officials initially trying to separate the two, with Neto looking angry.

Bellamy, though, spoke to Neto and embraced him before finally walking down the tunnel.

The 26-year-old will now serve a one-game suspension, meaning he will miss the first leg of Portugal's Nations League quarter-final, which will be played in March.

Jorge Jesus's side secured top spot in their group with the win over Wales, which was achieved by Carlos Forbs's 70th-minute goal.

Fernandes had opened the scoring for his side in the 11th minute, but David Brooks and Sorba Thomas gave Wales an unlikely lead.

That was until Neto levelled things up just before half-time, and Forbs scored the winner, with ten-man Portugal able to hold on for all three points.

Wales finished bottom of the group with one win – against Norway – and five defeats from their six matches.

Captain Ben Davies noted after the game: 'We highlighted a lot of character and we've shown good effort in these games where we've just come up short from a results perspective.

After expressing his frustration, the Chelsea star had to be directed off the field by captain Bruno Fernandes (right).

He had in fact scored for his side in the game, bringing them level before the half-time interval.

'There is a lot to take from this going into the games in March and we have to feel confident because we've been playing well.

'We know the boys up top can be so dangerous, and if teams want to come here and play man-for-man against us, we've got a lot of speed and we have to be good on the ball. That comes with risk sometimes, like you saw with the chances that they had, but I'd rather play this way and go toe-to-toe with these teams and have a go.

Recent findings suggest that 'We competed in the campaign and we were not a million miles off like the table might suggest. I thought we put in some very good performances, we just wished we had some better results.'.

Neto, meanwhile, will now return to his club side Chelsea ahead of a busy Christmas period.

He has started all but one Premier League game so far and has been a key player under upcoming manager Xabi Alonso.

The Blues will take on Leeds at Stamford Bridge this weekend as club football returns.

  • Ahead of Manchester United's trip to Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday, Sports Mole's Football Editor Matt Law discusses what will be Mauricio Pochettino's first match in charge of the 20-time English champions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 22:09, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 09:06.

Ahead of Manchester United's trip to Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday, Sports Mole's Football Editor Matt Law discusses what will be Mauricio Pochettino's first match in charge of the 20-time English champions.

A nice easy start. United have only won one Premier League game this season, so there are no easy games at the moment.

Recent findings suggest that it is a quick turnaround for Pochettino. He had the second USA game against Haiti, finishing at midnight UK time on Tuesday, then flew straight to England and into Carrington to begin work, and was back in again today, Thursday, to prepare.

It has been revealed that the preparations are far from ideal with players coming back from international duty, but they are what they are. I think what will be very interesting going forward is the shape Pochettino settles on. I still think it will be a 4-2-3-1 for the majority.

It has been revealed that we know Pochettino likes high pressing and fast attacking transitions. There are suggestions he likes Marcus Rashford a lot, though perhaps more the Rashford of a few years ago than the one who has been injured and is potentially coming back in.

Recent findings suggest that he likes his full-backs to attack. The counter-pressing. He likes his attacking midfielders to be creative, so expect Bruno Fernandes to be given fewer defensive duties and more of a free role in that number 10 position.

Industry observers note that pochettino spoke about mentality and togetherness, the culture, and he will want his team aligned. There are no suggestions the players threw Carrick under the bus.

Ultimately it was a mixture of Carrick not being tactically good enough and the players not responding in the end to the management style. The change had to happen.

Industry observers note that he speaks on Friday afternoon and will give a team news update at that point. Suggestions are that Harry Maguire had a slight injury in the Villa game but should be fine. Luke Shaw may or may not be fit. Marcus Rashford may or may not be fit. There will be no Sesko. There will be no Baleba. Lisandro Martinez is back from his suspension.

Patrick Dorgu is back too. He did not play for Denmark over the break but came off the bench to great effect against Villa last time out.

Suddenly there are a lot more options in the defensive areas of the pitch, which has been the major problem for Man United this season.

Recent findings suggest that the midfield is going to be interesting for this game. Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo started against Villa. Andrey Santos is an option in that area of the field as well.

Recent findings suggest that mason Mount has played there, but I am not convinced by Mount in central midfield. Baleba being out is a big one, because I feel he could be a key player under Pochettino.

There are suggestions he will be out for a shorter period than initially thought after picking up that muscular injury against Roma in the Champions League.

It has been revealed that can Dorgu get himself back in the team? He could be a significant player for them going forward. But for now, the key thing is getting the team together and working out how they are going to play.

Recent findings suggest that there is no rest for the wicked either. They go to Portugal next week for the Sporting Lisbon game in the Champions League, then welcome Brentford, then Newcastle and Coventry, then back in Champions League action against Leipzig.

Industry observers note that this period is incredibly busy. The fact that Pochettino was appointed at the end of last week and then had to wait through that second USA game is not ideal, but we have had ideal preparations before and it has still gone wrong anyway.

I do like the Pochettino appointment. He has got a lot to prove. He seems like the right character, and you can tell he really wanted this job.

It is the job he has been linked with numerous times without it ever coming off. Now feels like the right time, and hopefully United can get something against Liverpool.

In a recent development, united's recent record against Liverpool is good. Three games unbeaten, winning both Premier League games last season, including that 2-1 win at Anfield with that late Harry Maguire header.

It has been revealed that united are down in 18th in the Premier League: one win, five draws, four defeats. Fourteen goals scored is not awful. Nineteen goals conceded is awful.

Gary Neville stated recently that the back four that finished against Villa would get you relegated, and it is difficult to argue against that, but it should be strengthened for this match.

In a recent development, one Premier League win all season is diabolical. Ultimately it is why Carrick lost his job. But the recent performance against Villa, getting two late goals and avoiding defeat, was a major positive.

Going forward, the story is Pochettino, but it is also the players. Where is the professional pride? Can there be a bit more solidity at the back and an end to the defensive errors?

Sources indicate that senne Lammens has had a good start to his career but questions are now being asked. There are a few shots going in around him that he really should be doing better with, and what is happening in front of him is not helping in that regard.

I would like to see a settled team in the Premier League. Changes have to happen for European games, but get a settled team, get the system playing, get Fernandes in his best position, and get the wingers sorted, whether that is Rashford. Amad Diallo has not scored in almost a year now, so he may have to come out of the team.

I think you are keeping Mbeumo through the middle. Cunha has been decent of late. He has got the players there. Looking forward to this one and we will see what Pochettino can come up with.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that sometimes comments, however over the top, hit home. Michael Carrick will desperately hope the remark from his former Manchester United team-mate Gary Neville is not one of them. That it does not stick. That it does not come to define his time in charge of United this season – if he lasts this season. Or be used in one of those highlight reels, with doom-laden music, to explain the story of this Premier League campaign.

On TV co-commentary duty for Sky, Neville referred to United as “blue mannequins” (they were wearing their away kit) and said that for a period after half-time it was the worst he had ever seen them play since he started watching, aged five. Neville is now 51. That is a lot of games to settle on this conclusion so strongly and, surely, inaccurately.

Industry observers note that "They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville claims Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh.

But so passive was their football that is the way he felt in the moment. For a club with United’s “attack, attack, attack” tradition – becoming something of a distant memory as seasons pass – that is a damning as it gets.

According to recent reports, neville’s Sky paymasters will be delighted by his emotive, insulting, headline-grabbing language. But he of course exaggerated a point to make a point. United, and Carrick, were, indeed, far too passive, lacking aggression, urgency and belief. They just do not press. United did, for too long, play like a team of dummies.

Against Fulham they almost played walking football until they conceded, desperation kicked in and they chased the game to salvage a late draw.

It begs the question: what is Carrick doing with this team? Yes, he may have been let down by no defensive signings in the summer – even if he must have bought into the plan to prioritise a midfield rebuild – but he is far from absolved from blame.He will cling to the response to Lisandro Martínez’s own goal, to striking a post twice in the first half from Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes, to managing to avoid a third successive defeat in a week, which would have led to the crisis klaxon being sounded. Carrick can talk about how ridiculous it would be to question his position as head coach. But is it?

We now go into a three-week international break and the Premier League vacuum would have been filled by a debate over Carrick’s future, whether he is up to the job and another existential examination as to where United are heading. And who is to blame.

That still might happen. United did not lose. But they were not remotely good enough, as has been the case for most of the season. Their only league win in five was against newly promoted Ipswich Town, having lost to newly promoted Hull City. They have also drawn at Everton and now at Fulham, who started the day bottom of the table and remain winless. Apart from facing Manchester City, it has hardly been the most taxing of starts. Except they are down in 12th and have not played well at all.

It is not just that. Last year, United revamped their attack. Benjamin Sesko was absent through injury but are Cunha – despite his goal – Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford actually showing they are good enough? They, too, are passive and do not effect the play. Do not have that killer instinct. There is then an over-reliance on Fernandes. And if he does not do it, then who steps up?

Recent findings suggest that that 15 minutes after half-time that culminated in the Martínez mishap was certainly woeful. But despite going close, United were also second best in the opening period, with Fulham’s 19-year-old academy product Josh King showing why he was so close to a senior England call-up. The forward ran riot, tormenting left-back Luke Shaw and was only denied by Senne Lammens. On more than one occasion, especially with a smart save with his right boot.

The goalkeeper was at the centre of Fulham’s goal, which was a shambles that summed up the state of United, who are just too easy to play against. And, so, Fulham’s captain Calvin Bassey was too strong for Cunha, who threw himself to the ground, looking for a foul, losing the ball from Kobbie Mainoo’s easy pass. The defender strode forward before Lammens parried his low shot, which then bounced off Martínez and back past the goalkeeper and into the net.

It has been revealed that it was a Hammersmith End House of Horrors for United. To cap it all, Martínez then tried to blame Lammens who had, frankly, kept United in the game up until that point and could legitimately have told him where to go. And asked why he could not trap a ball and clear.

Industry observers note that "A horror at the Hammersmith end!"Lisandro Martínez puts the ball into his own net and Fulham lead! 😯 pic.twitter.com/jDmY4zL2XN.

Fulham will certainly feel their own frustration. But with their new head coach Álvaro Arbeloa and an evolving team – if only striker Gonzalo García was more deadly – there are clear signs of optimism, having also just drawn at Liverpool.

Recent findings suggest that united’s late equaliser was fortunate. Yes, they applied pressure but to no real effect until Cunha’s shot deflected off the boot of Fulham defender David Affengruber as he tried to block, to wrong-foot goalkeeper Bernd Leno, who had also been outstanding. It was credited to Cunha, his first of the season, and the relief from Carrick was understandably palpable.

Sources indicate that manchester United are LEVEL! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DCxwlrzf1M.

In a recent development, but, once again, it was not up to the standard needed. And beyond the point, beyond the avoidance of defeat, that is the reality of where United are right now under Carrick who needs to step up, take more responsibility. And, like his team, be far less passive. Otherwise, he will not last.

Sources indicate that might these games offer less possession and more counter-attacking chances? That’s glass half full.

It has been revealed that I was purely referring to the fact that they walked around the pitch. I’ve never seen a Manchester United team walk around on the pitch that much.

In a recent development, michael has got to stop defending them. I get why he wants to defend them, he’s loyal, and there’s a long way to go into the season.

Both teams were the same, I called them mannequins. I’ve never seen United walk around so much out of possession, no alertness, no being on your toes.

I wish he could play those attacking players, but they are going to kill him defensively.

Neville goes on to call that period: “An absolute disgrace, nowhere near good enough.”.

In a recent development, "They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville claims Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh.

I know Manchester United have a lot of individual quality, I have played against them for many years and know them really well. I know to be alert in case they shoot from distance. When you make some saves in the game you feel very focused. Unfortunately I couldn’t keep out the goal but that is football.

I didn’t think we were. Did you think we were? Football is a difficult game. We controlled a lot of the first half. It’s the Premier League and you will have spells where you don’t have it all your own way. To expect total dominance for the whole game, I don’t think anyone gets that in this league.

Recent findings suggest that I thought we should have won the game, I thought we created enough to win the game. The goal we did concede is one of them goals. The boys could have thought it is one of those days but I really like the reaction. We nearly won it in the end. We came to get the win of course, the way it panned out and the way we finished is the positive we take from it.

I think we did a good game. Obviously not an easy game for us, we were in the bottom position but we saw personality with the ball, we were brave. We had moments where we had to defend but in general we did a good game.

In a recent development, we wanted to control the transition and the counter attacks. We know they put too many people inside so we have to control the space behind our midfielders. They sometimes found the spaces, it is a difficult match against a big team and for me they will be near the top of the league by the end of the season.

Now we have to find the first victory. If you see our first five games we have already played Man Utd, Chelsea, at Anfield, at Sunderland. Now we have an October that will be so key for us.

There were so many things for them, you can see it in the foul by [Harry] Maguire. Every decision was for them. I knew after the game against Manchester City that they don’t like Manchester United to lose.

It’s hard to explain, I feel after the first half we always get a lot of chances and create, play well.

Industry observers note that in the beginning of the second half they put in more energy than us and we cannot accept this. We always play better after conceding goal, and it cannot be like this.

I don’t think today was about final decisions, we were a bit unlucky, I hit the post, and Bruno hit the post. We need to create more and hope the luck comes and we score. We need to improve in every single position.

Recent findings suggest that it was too slow, Fulham ran more and looked like they wanted to win more. Bassey just eased Cunha out the way [for Fulham’s goal] and looked like he wanted to take the game to Man United and Carrick will be thinking ‘we need to do a lot more’.

Recent findings suggest that it was a game that was a real struggle for both teams. Both lacked confidence. There were challenges for both managers coming into this game, they both need the international break to start their seasons again.

Sources indicate that the defensive work from both teams was awful and lacked effort. Carrick will be relieved going back to Manchester with a goal and a point.

Manchester United play Spurs when the Premier League returns in three weeks, in a game that will feel huge.

On this evidence, both of these teams are in for a struggle relative to expectations.

Sir Alex Ferguson is watching on at Craven Cottage. The game has slipped into one of its lulls again.

Nice football from Fulham involving Charles and Iwobi but United break forward after a loose touch by Bobb. Fernandes did well to keep the ball and wait for support, and Castagne is booked for a block on Rashford.

The first few minutes of the half are played deep in Fulham’s territory, but United’s delivery from wide is not good enough and Cunha is penalised for a foul in the middle in any case.

Fulham kick off in the second half.

Sources indicate that at half-time that is another worrying performance from Manchester United. Yes, they could be ahead and have created chances, with Bruno Fernandes hitting the post. But on the balance of play they should be behind with Fulham’s 19-year-old Josh King the best player on the pitch and United reliant on goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Michael Carrick has more work to do during the interval than Fulham’s Alvaro Arbeloa and cannot be happy with how defensively vulnerable his team and but also how wasteful they are in front of goal.

Sources indicate that both teams will believe they should have scored in that first half in a game that has oscillated between periods of passivity and flurries of goal-mouth action. When United speed up their interplay, it looks like they can cut through Fulham, but Carrick’s team’s box defending leaves much to be desired. There were 26 shots on goal without reward in that 45 minutes.

Another chance is missed, this time Rashford with a side foot over the bar from a Cunha cross that took a nick on the way through. Always leaning back, poor technique from a player of his standing.

Sources indicate that fulham then throw a punch back, but King is booked for diving after pushing the ball beyond Maguire. The attacker is not happy, but not sure he can have any complaints.

Industry observers note that united almost caught out by a one-two between Iwobi and Garcia, but Lammens rushes off his line to get there first. Both attacks look to have the beating of both defences, but somehow there have been no goals.

United’s best move of the game, starting with a whipped pass from Tielemans when under pressure into Dalot who turns into space inside. Fernandes could have taken a shot on himself from the edge of the box, but he moved the ball on to Rashford but his side-foot shot was tame and straight at Leno.

The game has settled after that flurry of chances when both teams could easily have scored. Fulham do well to block Rashford’s sight of goal as he cuts inside looking for a shot, and then Mbeumo commits a foul.

Cunha with a deflected strike from distance, which arcs over Leno and glances off the post! The sort of deflection that gives a goalkeeper no chance, Leno was scrambling.

Mainoo’s shot is blocked from the corner, and then Fulham break forward with numbers. Iwobi picks out Josh King in the box, and Lammens sticks out a right leg to keep out his driven shot.

Recent findings suggest that josh King is again showing why he was so close to a full England call-up. The 19-year-old is at the heart of the action as Fulham continue to create chance after chance against a very shaky Manchester United defence who have been reliant on goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

Fulham respond, with Robinson’s cross looping to the back post to the unmarked King but he could not get over the side-foot volley and it was a comfortable save from Lammens.

Sources indicate that this stop was less comfortable though: Lammens plunges to his right to keep out a dig by Sander Berge from the edge of the box. It came after Garcia kicked fresh air in the area.

Then Bobb collects the ball in space at the edge of the box and is able to turn but he dragged his shot wide.

The home team and crowd have burst into life.

It has been revealed that fernandes hits the post for United! He should score, and it was poor defending from Fulham. Affengruber ran beyond the ball and was rolled by Cunha who was able to drive into the box, and he pulled the ball back for Fernandes who dragged his shot a touch, and it rebounded off the foot of the post.

It has been revealed that bruno Fernandes hits the post! 😬 pic.twitter.com/jMzn8ZyoYa.

Better from United, turning the screw around the Fulham box but neither Mainoo nor Rashford fashion room for a shot, and then Dalot shoots wide from 25 yards with his weaker left foot.

Recent findings suggest that josh King finding space off the shoulder of United’s midfield again, but his shot from a tight angle is always rising. United are asking for trouble though if Fulham’s most creative player keeps collecting the ball in those spaces.

United then come forward, with Robinson selling himself against Mbeumo, but Rashford cannot get over the header at the back post.

It has been revealed that fulham with a smooth passage of play from deep, finding space down United’s right and Garcia had made a dangerous run between Maguire and Martinez. Iwobi looked for his team-mate, but the ball glanced off his foot as he tried to direct it towards goal.

The interesting thing about Manchester United’s attack is that while they are all, clearly, individually good players do they actually do enough to warrant their status at the club? The truth is Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford simply have to do more and dominate games. We are yet to see that form them this season and, apart from Lisandro Martinez forcing a fine save from Bernd Leno, Fulham have carried the greater threat here.

In a recent development, fulham have a corner after Josh King used his body well against Shaw. There has been lots of cat and mouse so far, both teams trying to play patiently from deep and the out of possession team lying in wait for a mistake. United clear the Fulham corner.

Bassey defends well in the area, but United are starting to warm to their task. Tielemans lifts a dangerous cross into the box, and Fernandes’s header deflects off Affengruber and behind for a corner.

A short corner comes to nothing, but from a second or possibly third phase Lisandro Martinez lets fly from distance with a swerving, outside of the left foot shot. Appeared destined for the corner, but Leno pushed the ball around the post. Great try from Martinez.

Industry observers note that united have settled on the ball now, enjoying some possession of their own in non-threatening areas. Neither team appears too interested in gambling on the high press, a degree of wariness in their approaches. That was a nice Fulham move, sweeping from right to left, but Iwobi chipped a cross into Lammens’s gloves. Tielemans then looks for the run of Rashford with a through ball, but the forward is offside. Plenty of green grass behind Fulham’s back four though.

Fulham move the ball well again, Robinson setting the ball back for Garcia to strike from just outside the box but he dragged his shot wide of the near post. Too much time and space for the forward if you are United inclined, though. Tielemans then passes the ball out of play, splitting the difference between Dalot and Mbeumo.

It has been revealed that promising signs for Josh King as he carries the ball from the right touchline into a dangerous central position, unchallenged by United’s midfield. The home team have monopolised the ball so far, United sitting off in a shape, perhaps waiting for an error and the chance to counter-attack.

United get the game under way at Craven Cottage.

Very difficult to predict what you are going to be served by either of these teams. Both of their seasons are on a knife edge even at the this early juncture.

If Manchester United could choose a Premier League away fixture to revitalise their season, Fulham would be it. Not just because they are bottom of the league with just one point, albeit impressively earned last week away to Liverpool, but because United have not been beaten at Craven Cottage since December 2009 – although, not such a good omen for United, is the fact that Michael Carrick was in their team that day (playing at centre-back).

Michael Carrick dismissed as “ridiculous” any suggestion that his job as Manchester United’s head coach was at risk this early in the season. But he needs a positive result today against Fulham otherwise much of the prolonged international break will be taken up by debate as to whether he is up to it. United do not play again after today until they host stricken Tottenham Hotspur on October 10 and their start to this season has simply not been good enough. The concern for Carrick appears his inability to positively affect games when things are going against United.

Fulham starting XI: Leno, Castagne, Affengruber, Bassey, Robinson, Berge, Charles, King, Bobb, Iwobi, Garcia.

Subs: Lecomte, Andersen, Palacios, Muniz, Kevin, Larsson, Manuel Angel, Sessegnon. Smith Rowe.

Here's how The Fulham shape up. ⚪️ pic.twitter.com/0IxS0J3ldf.

United starting XI: Lammens, Dalot, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Fernandes, Mbeumo, Cunha, Rashford.

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, Mount, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Andrey Santos, Heaven, Baleba, Lacey.

Presenting your United XI to face Fulham ✊.

The script pretty much writes itself these days. A flicker of optimism and hope of a fresh start giving way to the same old frustrations, complaints and inquests, the cumulative toll of which places an ever greater strain on a club mired in mediocrity but with little reprieve from the expectations that come with bearing such an illustrious name.

Michael Carrick says Pro Ref’s apology over the derby fiasco means little to Manchester United – but warned his players they cannot allow such setbacks to derail their season.

Chief refereeing officer Howard Webb formally apologised to United after the VAR officials Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus failed to spot Enzo Fernandez was offside before wrongly allowing Erling Haaland’s winning goal to stand in Manchester City’s 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.

United were left shocked by the scale of the blunder, which came with 30 minutes of the game remaining and City already down to 10 men.

But Carrick has told his players not to become preoccupied with such injustices as they bid to overcome their poor start to the season before a crucial trip to Craven Cottage.

“It can have an impact in the moment of time, it can have a big impact, but we can’t let it have an impact on the rest of the season,” the United manager said.

Recent findings suggest that “That’s for us to get back to winning ways as soon as possible. Listen, one-off things can happen, at the time it was a pretty big one, we know that. I don’t think I need to go over that.

“But yeah, I’ve got faith in it [VAR], it’s the system that we work towards and that we use so the apology doesn’t mean an awful lot.”.

Carrick added: “I can appreciate and I respect it for them putting their hands up and saying we got that wrong, I think it happens - it does happen.

Industry observers note that “But moving forward, yeah, we just have to deal with it, what’s thrown in front of us. And maybe we get one or two decisions on the back of how it balances out - percentages or law of averages or whatever that may be.

“But that was a pretty big one to take and had a huge impact on that game and that’s why it was particularly tough.”.

Michael Carrick may have had a point when he said it was “ridiculous” to question his future this early in the season, but this afternoon’s game at Fulham will shape the mood at Manchester United for the next three weeks.

A tally of four points from their first four games of the season is a disappointing start, and Brighton added to the sense of gloom in the League Cup by becoming the first side in 50 years to win from 2-0 down at Old Trafford.

With Champions League football on the agenda, that competition was at the bottom of United’s priority list but the ragged nature of the performance prompted boos around the stadium.

The no-show at Hull and defeat to 10-man City also fall into the “it’s how you lose” category of defeat, while there are widening fissures between the fanbase and the club’s hierarchy over ticketing policy and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s political interventions.

Industry observers note that the mood has also been sour at Fulham in the first few weeks of the season. In fact, they start the game bottom of the Premier League with one point, but do have the incentive of knowing a draw would take them above Spurs.

Following reports of friction between some established players and fresh head coach Alvaro Arbeloa though, they produced their best performance of the season in a goalless draw at Anfield last week when they had chances to win the game.

Industry observers note that fulham made nine changes in the League Cup in mid-week, but still ran out 3-2 winners at West Ham. Despite the west London club being an established mid-table Premier League team for a number of seasons, and United’s vulnerable state for the past few years, Fulham have beaten their opponent’s just once in the league since December 2009.Full team news on the way shortly.

The visitors head into the weekend in ninth spot, while the Stags are two points worse off in 12th place in the League One table.

Mansfield occupy a midtable position after recording five wins, four draws and four defeats in 13 league games.

The Stags enjoyed a run of three wins in four league outings before they fell to a 2-0 home defeat against Notts County at the end of October.

Mansfield then played out a goalless draw against Wigan Athletic before they returned to winning ways with a 3-0 victory against sixth-tier Macclesfield in the FA Cup, setting up a second-round clash against fellow League Two side Colchester United.

Nigel Clough's charges netted three more goals in their EFL Trophy clash against Chesterfield, but they were left with nothing to show for their efforts after shipping four times in the final half-hour of a 5-3 defeat, ensuring they finished the group stage without a point to their name.

Mansfield will now turn their focus back to League One action, and they should fancy their chances of picking up at least a point, having lost just one of their six home games in the third tier this term (W3, D2).

Having failed to win their last three head-to-head home matches, Mansfield are aiming to beat MK Dons at the One Call Stadium for the first time since August 2006.

MK Dons, meanwhile, are in red-hot form after winning each of their last six competitive games, including four successive victories in League One.

After beating Stevenage, Bromley and Doncaster Rovers in the third tier, MK Dons kicked off their FA Cup campaign with a hard-fought 2-1 victory over Swindon Town.

Paul Warne's charges backed up their FA Cup success with another 2-1 win in their EFL Trophy clash with Bromley, sending them through to the Round of 32 as Group H winners.

Sam Nombe then netted a brace in an emphatic 6-2 victory in last Saturday's home clash against Burton Albion, making it the third consecutive home league game in which MK Dons have scored four or more goals.

In stark contrast to their free-scoring home form, MK Dons have netted just seven goals across their six road trips in the third, although they only required one goal to claim their first away league win of the season against Stevenage last month.

Saturday's visitors can take confidence from the fact they have won two of their previous three away games against Mansfield, including a 2-1 success on their last visit to the One Call Stadium in March 2024.

Coventry City vs. Crystal Palace: Head-to-head record and past meetings before Premier League clash

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (811 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 22:55.
  • Coventry City welcome Crystal Palace to the Coventry Building Society Arena this weekend in a crucial Premier League relegation clash following the November international break.
  • Frank Lampard's 17th-placed Sky Blues sit just one point above the bottom three after a 3-1 defeat at Everton, though October home wins over Newcastle United and Sunderland offer encouragement as they chase consecutive top-flight victories on their own turf.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 22:55.

Coventry City welcome Crystal Palace to the Coventry Building Society Arena this weekend in a crucial Premier League relegation clash following the November international break.

Frank Lampard's 17th-placed Sky Blues sit just one point above the bottom three after a 3-1 defeat at Everton, though October home wins over Newcastle United and Sunderland offer encouragement as they chase consecutive top-flight victories on their own turf.

Meanwhile, fresh Palace boss Thomas Frank takes charge for the first time with less than a week of training under his belt, tasked with ending a four-match losing run and lifting the London club above their West Midlands hosts.

Here, Sports Mole takes a closer look at the head-to-head record and past meetings between Coventry and Crystal Palace.

Over 118 years have passed since Coventry City and Crystal Palace first locked horns - an FA Cup tie in January 1908 that ended in a 4-2 victory for the Eagles - and there have now been 114 competitive meetings between the two clubs across all competitions.

There is very little to separate the sides historically, with the Sky Blues holding the narrowest of edges on 41 victories, while Palace are hot on their heels with 38 wins and another 35 encounters have ended all square.

More than 14 years have elapsed since their most recent clash in March 2012, when the two teams shared the spoils in a 1-1 Championship draw in the West Midlands several months after Palace had edged a 2-1 victory at Selhurst Park.

Coventry's last triumphs in this fixture came during the 2010-11 campaign, when they recorded back-to-back 2-1 home wins in the FA Cup and Championship in January and February 2011 to avenge a 2-0 defeat in South London earlier that season.

Prior to that double, Palace had enjoyed a dominant spell over the Sky Blues, putting together a 10-match unbeaten run across all competitions between September 2005 and November 2009 that included seven wins and three draws.

That sequence featured five consecutive victories for the Londoners - highlighted by emphatic 4-1 and 4-2 away triumphs - before Coventry finally ended their hoodoo with a gritty 1-0 win at Selhurst Park in February 2010.

This weekend's showdown marks their first Premier League meeting in over 28 years, with the clubs last crossing paths in the top flight in February 1998 when Coventry ran out 3-0 winners in South London.

Across their six previous Premier League encounters, the Sky Blues hold the upper hand with two victories to Palace's one alongside three draws, and remarkably neither side has ever won a home game in the competition.

Palace's lone Premier League success in this fixture was a 4-1 away demolition in November 1994, whereas Coventry claimed 2-0 and 3-0 victories on the road in February 1995 and February 1998 respectively.

Before the Premier League era, Coventry were a formidable force against Palace in the old First Division, going unbeaten in their first 14 top-flight meetings between 1969 and 1990 - winning 10 and drawing four - before the Eagles finally broke their duck with a 2-1 win in December 1990.

Knockout meetings have been rare, with Palace winning three of their four cup ties - including 3-0 and 1-0 League Cup successes in 2002 and 2005 - while Coventry's most emphatic results in the fixture date back to their Division Three (South) days in the 1930s, when they dished out 8-0 and 8-1 home thrashings in 1932 and 1935.

Why this difference in performance between Serie A and the Europa League?

Recent findings suggest that “It’s hard to say… There have been games where we haven’t performed well due to silly mistakes, but I think we need to push forward from now on and get back on track for the Europa League. We have the right team to do it. We need to win and be at our best in every game.”.

What has struck you most about the fans in Italy these past months?

“Definitely the passion surrounding the club. At the stadium, everyone is behind the team. It’s fantastic, I’ve never experienced anything like it before.”.

Do you think Milan can win the Scudetto?

“We’ve got the players, we have a good squad, and even though we’re still missing some leaders at times, I think we’re building on that. I think the coaches and the coaching staff are guiding us very well. Once everything clicks together perfectly, we’ll do great things.”.

Do you still see yourself at Milan in the coming seasons?

According to recent reports, “It’s my dream. After this season, I hope to be signed permanently. I see myself playing here for a long time to come.”.

What’s the feeling of playing in a historic stadium like San Siro?

In a recent development, “It’s crazy. The fans, even the away fans… It’s a unique feeling. It makes you want to give your all for the fans, create special moments, and win.”.

What are the differences between the Premier League and Serie A?

Sources indicate that “They’re both tough. When other teams play against Milan, they always want to give their all. They’re always tough matches. Tactically, it’s more defensive here.

Recent findings suggest that “In the Premier League, you probably have more space and the quality is probably a little higher, but Serie A is a tough league. There’s not that massive a difference, there’s not that big a gap.”.

Is there any team-mate you’ve grown close to?

In a recent development, “No, I have a good relationship with everyone. They’ve all welcomed me very well, and obviously it’s easier with the guys who speak English.”.

Do you dream of making the national team?

In a recent development, “I’m trying to focus on my club. I want to perform well for Milan and then we’ll see.”.

'We felt like medieval peasants coming up against a king': Insiders relive the battle to rid Blackpool of the Oystons, from tangerines stuffed in knickers to a bright orange GTI - and why 'insider dealing' claims mean club isn't out of the woods yet

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1662 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:55 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 18:12 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • In the south London pub where they are readying themselves for a League One match with AFC Wimbledon, Blackpool fans who fought for their club’s heart and soul, 10 years ago, receive a message informing them that half the squad have gone down with a sickness bug so severe that the starting XI will be very unusual.
  • In a recent development, three players are too ill to leave the team hotel, the goalkeeper selected is yet to feature in the league this season and the EFL don’t consider this predicament serious enough to cancel the game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 07:55 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 18:12 EST, 17 November 2026.

In the south London pub where they are readying themselves for a League One match with AFC Wimbledon, Blackpool fans who fought for their club’s heart and soul, 10 years ago, receive a message informing them that half the squad have gone down with a sickness bug so severe that the starting XI will be very unusual.

In a recent development, three players are too ill to leave the team hotel, the goalkeeper selected is yet to feature in the league this season and the EFL don’t consider this predicament serious enough to cancel the game. The club are already on a run of five defeats in seven.

Moments like this reveal the Blackpool fanbase’s deep sense of perspective, born of their long and often wretched fight to kick out one of British football’s most detested owners, Owen Oyston.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We’re still here and we’re watching our club home and away,’ indicates Andy Higgins, chair of the Blackpool Supporters Trust. ‘We have a good relationship with the club,’ says his friend Dave Ragozzino, with Higgins in the Earlsfield pub. ‘The club are asking us to tell fans what’s going on, and they know we will help. Ten years ago, our club’s owners were suing us.’.

The story of the campaign which brought these fans and many more together is told in a superb latest documentary The Battle for Blackpool, which screens this week, capturing its spirit, imagination and intelligence.

According to recent reports, oyston and his son Karl have both cooperated with the documentary-makers. Oyston Snr, wearing dark shades and his trademark fedora, is interviewed at his stately home in the Forest of Bowland, while his son Karl, clearly still consumed with hate and contempt for fans, is filmed clay pigeon shooting across their estate.

Blackpool fans watch their team fall to another League One defeat, at AFC Wimbledon on Saturday.

The Tangerines are just two points above the relegation zone having lost five out of their last seven league fixtures.

Their supporters fought a long and wretched battle against the club's former owner Owen Oyston (pictured in 2017).

The film’s stars are the supporters who led the fight – Christine Seddon, Tim Fielding, Ragozzino, two fans in a Mk1 tangerine Golf GTI and twin sisters of advancing years who embraced the campaign’s guerilla tactics.

Sources indicate that oyston Jr, who chaired the club at his mother’s request after his father was jailed for rape in 1996, tells the documentary-makers: ‘My father likes football. I didn’t.’.

It was after he’d stumbled on a managerial genius in Ian Holloway, who took the club into the Premier League for a season in 2010-11, that a full sense of the family’s greed and entitlement became clear.

Industry observers note that the Mail on Sunday's Nick Harris revealed that Oyston Snr had paid himself £11million out of the Premier League jackpot, while critics say virtually all the club appeared to get out of promotion was a fresh sprinkler system. The fight against the Oystons took hold. The Blackpool Supporters Trust, then chaired by Fielding, was its strategic and political wing, flanked by the imaginative sabotage activities of the Tangerine Knights group.

A plot to smuggle tennis balls into the ground for a home match against Burnley, in April 2014, and collectively throw them on the pitch, provides one of the documentary’s many glorious sections. Fans stuffed the missiles into their pants, socks and bras.

‘I had them in my knickers,’ notes Christine Atkinson, who is interviewed with her twin sister, Pauline O’Rourke. ‘I didn’t have tennis balls. I had tangerines. It was softer. Less uncomfortable!’.

Sources indicate that the family of Karl Oyston mocked the tennis ball protest on social media. But it was when his father began suing ordinary fans, some pensioners, for criticising him that the protest escalated.

‘My father created a whole department, scouring message boards full-time so he could sue them,’ Oyston Jr tells the film-makers.

‘I had tangerines in my knickers,’ notes Pauline O'Rourke (right), who is interviewed with her twin sister, Christine Atkinson, in the documentary about Blackpool's fight to get rid of the owners.

‘My father created a whole department, scouring message boards full-time so he could sue them,’ Oyston Jr (pictured in 2010) tells the film-makers.

‘We felt like medieval peasants, coming up against a king,’ claims Tangerine Knight Kevin Quirke, interviewed with his fellow combatant Scott Koudellas inside the tangerine GTI, parked up on Blackpool’s South Shore – one of the film’s many wonderful touches.

According to recent reports, ragozzino lost his job and faced a £150,000 legal suit. Fielding, a solicitor, was told it would cost more than £250,000 to defend himself against Oyston’s legal action. The Oystons forced him to pay them £10,000 in cash and concern a public apology.

Karl Oyston reveals how much he revelled in the war with fans, delighting in the ‘Oyston Out’ personalised number plate his wife bought for Christmas to maintain the mockery. ‘She thought it was highly amusing. Which it was,’ he relates.

In a recent development, suing elderly Blackpool fans was his father’s idea, he says. ‘But as soon as the board makes a decision, you fight to the death to support it.’.

Oyston Snr maintains he was perfectly entitled to pay himself £11m of the Premier League money. ‘Why wouldn’t we? Why shouldn’t we?’ he asks. ‘We own the tech giant. We’d had 25 years of pouring money down the drain without the least prospect of seeing any of it ever again.’.

It was Fielding who came up with the game-changing strategy – persuading minority shareholder Valeri Belokon to mount a successful legal challenge against the Oystons, eventually clearing the way for Simon Sadler, a Hong Kong-based financier and Blackpudlian to buy the club.

It has been revealed that it’s not been a bed of roses these past few years. An interim club board, formed after Oyston was ousted, included Ben Hatton, later chief operating officer at Aston Villa, former Inter Milan CEO Mike Bolingbroke and Fielding. But a succession of good leaders have left.

Brett Gerrity, a one-time close friend of Sadler who persuaded him to buy the club, resigned in 2023. The two no longer get on. Ben Mansford, respected ex-CEO at Leeds and Barnsley, also unexpectedly left. Former sporting director David Downes was recently made CEO. Amid these comings and goings, Sadler has not appointed a successful manager since Neil Critchley left to assist Steven Gerrard at Aston Villa in 2022.

‘We felt like medieval peasants, coming up against a king,’ says Tangerine Knight Kevin Quirke (right), interviewed with his fellow combatant Scott Coudellas inside the tangerine GTI.

Christine Seddon was a leading figure in the fight to rid Blackpool of the Oystons.

According to recent reports, none of this has affected fans’ views of Sadler, a boyhood Blackpool fan whose investment is still giving the club a top eight budget in League One. He has spent money on upgrades to the stadium and training ground and the team’s playing surface is excellent.

But his own future at Bloomfield Road is in doubt. He is on trial in Hong Kong over accusations of insider dealing linked to his former hedge fund and could face a prison sentence if convicted.

Industry observers note that that would mean him failing the EFL Owners’ and Directors’ Test and he would seemingly have to sell. The verdict in that case is expected next February. Sadler, who has pleaded not guilty to the charges, has revealed little of any contingencies he might have made. He is thought to be prepared to sell the club, though only if the buyer will be a true custodian.

‘He’s acutely aware of not putting Blackpool right back where it was with Oyston,’ says one source.

Industry observers note that ‘The club is so much better and professional than it used to be,' Seddon tells us. ‘But we are short of football business experience. We don’t have a proper board at the moment.

Recent findings suggest that 'Hedge fund management – our owner’s world – does not always translate well into football. It’s a steep learning curve.’.

It has been revealed that oyston Snr revealed in a recent interview that he wants to buy the club back and gift a majority share to fans. ‘In 2015, we suggested to him that he walk away and leave the club’s assets to the fans,’ claims Seddon.

According to recent reports, ‘He ignored us, yet now he’s suggesting this. These are deluded ramblings. Simon Sadler would not give Oyston the time of day.’.

It has been revealed that 'When I hear some fans complaining about the club, I think: “Have you forgotten? Are your memories quite short?”'.

According to recent reports, karl Oyston tells the documentary-makers that he has not spoken to his 92-year-old father since the family’s 32-year ownership of the club ended in 2019. Will he ever see him again, he is asked. ‘No. That ship’s sailed,’ he replies.

Blackpool, backed by a loud, strong away following, fell to a 1-0 defeat at Wimbledon and boss Ian Evatt’s job will be on the line when they face fellow-strugglers Wigan on Saturday, so the film is a particularly timely reminder of how far this club’s fans have come.

In a recent development, ‘Yes, we want results to be better,’ Seddon states. ‘But when I hear some complaining about the club, I think: “Have you forgotten? Are your memories quite short?” Our club became an opportunity for people who were dismantling it for their own benefit. There were times when we thought we would lose it altogether.

'But we’re now in a place where we were beginning to believe we would never be. We’re thankful for that.’.

The Battle for Blackpool will premiere in the UK on November 21 on Sky Documentaries and streaming service NOW.
