Sir Jim Ratcliffe has only made the situation at Manchester United worse since his arrival.

That is the opinion of experienced former Tottenham, Everton and Aston Villa scout, Bryan King, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

INEOS, led by the billionaire, became minority owners of the Red Devils in 2024, and have since been in control of the majority football operations.

Ratcliffe was involved in the decision to dismiss Michael Carrick last week, but had reportedly wanted Eddie Howe appointed to replace him.

Majority owners, the Glazer family, are remarked to have overruled him by appointing Mauricio Pochettino instead.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss will take charge for the first time on Sunday, when Man United visit Liverpool at Anfield.

Pochettino will hope to bring stability to Man United, but he will need to get those above him on board.

Manager after manager has failed at Old Trafford, with the board and the ownership seemingly incapable of creating a good environment.

Industry observers note that "I just think that the whole palaver here will end in tears, and I hope it does," King told Football Insider. "I really hope it does.

It has been revealed that "Because the way they've gone about running that football club for the last 10 years is diabolical. Ever since Ratcliffe came in, it's gone from one bit of chaos to the next.

"What you have to look at here is the way he and his company are running it. Great businessman, but football as a business is, you have to have a totally different approach to the way you're running your own company, INEOS.

Recent findings suggest that "You can't take that strategy into a football club like Man United. Through him, the people that have gone, and he's got rid of a lot of people, the newly introduced people he's brought in are certainly not up to the job.

"So why are they still there? And they are still there. Now he's replaced Carrick and at least six members of staff at God knows what cost, and he's bringing in this fella who's going to be on massive wages, by the way.".

Pochettino has insisted that he has the support of those above him at Man United.

"I feel all the support. We feel all the support from the directors and the owners," the Argentine said after his appointment was confirmed.

"And of course, now it's up to us to provide what they expect from us.

"We have clear idea what the club expect from us and we want to be in the level of the demand of this football club.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 02:51, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 05:04.

Hoping to solidify their spot in the top half of the Scottish Premiership, Dundee United will travel to face Hibernian at Easter Road Stadium.

The Hibees are keen to pick up where they left off with a win, while the Tangerines could make it eight games unbeaten.

Marink Reedijk's Hibs have endured a difficult campaign to date, and fans will be looking to see a rejuvenated team emerge on their return from the international break.

The Hibees went winless throughout the entirety of October, and by the end of the month had racked up a total of six matches without a victory, losing four times in the process.

However, Reedijk's side came from behind to beat Hearts 2-1 in the Scottish League Cup semi-final on November 1, courtesy of goals from Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath.

That Edinburgh Derby success may have marked a turning point for Hibs, who went on to thrash Aberdeen 4-0 in the Scottish Premiership six days later, McGrath once again decisive as he netted the opener early in the second half.

Earning a first league win since August 30 has left the Hibees 10th in the table with 11 points after 12 games, from where they could climb up to eighth given that Motherwell and St Mirren are set to play Rangers and Celtic respectively this weekend.

On the other hand, Reedijk's men remain just two points above bottom-of-the-table Kilmarnock, and with five defeats to go with a single draw from their six most recent home clashes, it would take a shock for the hosts to prevail on Saturday.

Meanwhile, Jim Goodwin's Dundee Utd have their sights set on cementing their place in the top six, and this weekend's trip to Easter Road could be crucial.

The Tangerines are right now sixth with 17 points, level with city rivals Dundee in fifth and just three points behind fourth-placed Hearts.

That being said, Goodwin's side will be looking over their shoulder at seventh-placed St Johnstone - who they are also level on points with - and eighth-placed St Mirren, who are just three points behind.

Considering that Saturday's result may be directionally significant for Dundee Utd, fans will take heart from the fact the team arrive on the back of a seven-game unbeaten streak after their 1-1 draw with Motherwell on November 7, not to mention that the Tangerines have lost just one of their last five away clashes.

However, it is notable that the visitors' undefeated run features four draws alongside three wins, and it remains to be seen whether they can secure maximum points against a potentially resurgent Hibs on home turf.

Dundee United Scottish Premiership form:.

Hibernian are without right-back options Felix Passlack and Kanayochukwu Megwa due to respective hamstring and thigh problems, while centre-back Rocky Bushiri remains sidelined with an Achilles injury.

With that in mind, Alex Williams could start on the right of a four-man defence featuring Jason Kerr, Marko Ivezic and Jack Iredale in front of goalkeeper Raphael Sallinger.

At the opposite end of the pitch, striker Nathan Lowe is out injured, so 20-year-old Owen Elding is likely to operate up top, supported by Josh Mulligan and Martin Boyle from out wide.

As for Dundee Utd, they are missing right-sided attacker Neil Farrugia due to a groin injury, though Jesse Randall should be on hand to start as part of a trio alongside Dylan Tait and Daniel Bennie behind Zachary Sapsford.

Left-back Will ferry is also dealing with a muscle injury, while midfielder Emmanuel Agyei is recovering from a knee problem.

In their absence, Kevin Ciubotaru looks set to start on the left side of the visiting defence, with Lyall Cameron and Zidane Iqbal forming Goodwin's double pivot.

Hibernian possible starting lineup:.

Sallinger; Williams, Kerr, Ivezic, Iredale; Chaiwa, Newell; Mulligan, McGrath, Boyle; Elding.

Dundee United possible starting lineup:.

Walton; Rawlins, Esselink, Forbes, Ciubotaru; Cameron, Iqbal; Randall, Tait, Bennie; Sapsford.

Hibernian have struggled this term and are sat near the bottom of the table, but their results picked up prior to the international break, and they will be motivated to continue their burgeoning resurgence under Reedijk.

Dundee Utd have proven resilient so far and their unbeaten streak is unlikely to be broken at Easter Road, though they could fall short of winning on Saturday.

By Lewis Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 02:54, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:03.

Liverpool's Premier League campaign resumes at Anfield on Sunday, when they take on fierce rivals Manchester United.

The hosts come into the clash in fourth place with 18 points after 10 matchweeks, whereas United are in 18th place with just eight points.

Andoni Iraola will know the importance of winning at Anfield considering he has already lost against Manchester City and Arsenal, and he cannot afford a loss against the Red Devils at their lowest moment.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up Liverpool’s latest injury and suspension news ahead of their Premier League fixture against Man United.

© Imago / David Rawcliffe, Propaganda Photo.

Possible return date: November 22 (vs. Manchester United).

Ryan Gravenberch was left on the bench against Arsenal on November 1, and he was left out of the squad that faced Fenerbahce three days later.

Iraola confirmed that he was dealing with a fracture in his foot, though despite missing his side's win against Crystal Palace before the November international break, he could make his return against Man United.

© Iconsport / Marty Jean-Louis/Sipa USA.

According to recent reports, possible return date: November 22 (vs. Manchester United).

Speedster Jeremie Frimpong was brought on at half time against Brentford on October 17 but had to be replaced just seven minutes later with a hamstring injury.

Recent findings suggest that the right-back is set to be sidelined until after the international break, and Iraola stated on October 19, "It’s going to be difficult, I think, before the [November international] break. We will try but it's going to be difficult to have him.".

Frimpong did not return before the break, but he could return to the squad against Man United.

Possible return date: December 26 (vs. Hull City).

Striker Hugo Ekitike has been out of action since rupturing his Achilles against Paris Saint-Germain in April, and is going through rehabilitation following surgery on the tear.

The Frenchman is unlikely to take to the pitch for some weeks, but has been included in Liverpool's squad for the Champions League league-phase, and could return during the festive period.

Recent findings suggest that possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City).

Nineteen-year-old centre-back Giovanni Leoni is another long-term absentee for Liverpool, having suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury on his debut in September 2025.

Speaking on October 15, Iraola revealed that the defender has faced a setback, saying, "It’s taking more time than we wanted. The plan was to train with the team in this past international break [but] probably it’s going to be in the next [one].".

The defender has since returned to parts of team training, though he is far behind the rest of the squad.

According to recent reports, possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City).

Right-back Conor Bradley has been unavailable since picking up a major knee injury against Arsenal in January, though he is planning a return this autumn.

The academy graduate has yet to join team training, but is making progress in his rehabilitation and started doing ball work earlier this month.

Much like Leoni, the right-back has returned to parts of team training, but Liverpool are set to take a cautious approach to his fitness.

Liverpool have no players suspended for this match.

It has been revealed that the stars and stripes certainly gave him a fitting send-off, as they won the first leg 6-0 a few days ago and then completed the job with a 2-0 victory in Cincinnati last night. Pulisic got the first goal after a brace in the previous rout, and it was an incredible overhead kick.

Pulisic was actually overlooked by Pochettino for the September-October window – partly for fitness reasons – and he spoke to reporters after the game to share his thoughts after an emotional evening. He was called the ‘best player on the pitch’ by the US media, and his words are via MilanNews.

An overhead kick goal is pretty special….

It has been revealed that “I’ve never scored a goal like that, it was special. Weston crossed the ball and it was the only thing I could really do, so I thought I had to give it a try. It was really nice to see the ball go in.”.

Is it nice to get a victory on Pochettino’s farewell day?

“Yes, obviously he’s leaving now, so it’s nice to end with a good performance and a nice win for the team.”.

How would you describe this particular group, a mix of veterans and young players?

“It’s really nice. It’s been fun working with everyone. We got to meet some of the upcoming guys, even some young talent, and obviously there’s still some of the same core group, so it’s a really great team. I really like where we are right now and I think we’re still growing and have a great future ahead of us.”.

EVERY ANGLE OF THE PULISIC BICYCLE KICK 🎥 https://t.co/jFSFZx5Wan.

What does Pochettino’s last match leave you with?

Sources indicate that “We’re in a good place. Overall, I think the team has improved. I think there’s a good culture within the group, and I think we should be really excited about the future.”.

What kind of an impact has Julian Hall made?

“It was fantastic playing with him. He scored a goal, but also just for his overall play, making lots of runs and causing problems for the other team. He did a great job, fitting in with this team and making his mark.”.

What was Mauricio Pochettino’s farewell message to you this evening?

“Simply that we have a truly extraordinary culture. We’ve built something truly special and that a bright future awaits us. And to continue that by letting the rest of the team support us.”.

Does it really matter who the coach is at this point?

According to recent reports, “I mean, not that it doesn’t matter. Ultimately, it’s not our choice, as players. We hope whoever arrives will be able to capitalise on the things we do so well and lead us in the right direction.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 06:01 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 06:43 EST, 18 November 2026.

Manchester United have expressed their concern over the circumstances surrounding JJ Gabriel’s imminent move to Real Madrid, and threatened legal action if there is any evidence that he was induced to leave.

The 16-year-old winger posted a video on social media on Tuesday night confirming his departure from United as talks with Madrid continue between his new agent Ali Barat and close family at the club’s Valdebebas headquarters.

United sources say they are disappointed the video appeared without any contact with them, but the club will maintain its policy of not punishing Gabriel for what it sees as the actions of adults.

However, they have reiterated that United will fight with every legal means possible if any evidence of inducement from another club comes to light.

It’s understood that United have been unable to make contact with Gabriel – who has not been seen at the club since September – or his family despite numerous attempts to check on his welfare. They want an opportunity to ensure that he has a say in what could be a life-changing decision.

Gabriel has been training in Madrid and gave an interview to Marca earlier this month saying that he favoured a move to the 15-time European champions over rivals Barcelona, while expressing an ambition to win the Ballon d’Or.

Manchester United are prepared for a legal fight with Real Madrid over JJ Gabriel.

The youngster is on the verge of joining the Spanish giants in a controversial move.

It has been revealed that he is registered as a United player for the rest of the season and the club are refusing to tear up that agreement in the belief that he would still need approval from FIFA to make the move. However, sources stress that there has been no contact from any football authority seeking to de-register him.

Gabriel has been at United since the age of 11, and is considered one of the hottest young prospects in European football. He is registered with United's academy until the end of the season but Real Madrid are intending to sign him in January.

There is a FIFA loophole that allows European clubs to tie down young players to professional contracts if they have a European passport which Gabriel qualifies for through both parents.

It has been revealed that in a farewell post on Instagram he said: 'Dear Manchester United, I arrived in 2020. as a 10-year-old boy with substantial dreams.

According to recent reports, 'Here I grew as a player and as a person. From scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy Award.

'You gave me moments I'll always treasure. To every coach, every member of staff, to my team-mates and everyone who supported me, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow.

In a recent development, 'As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything. JJ.'.

Gabriel did not make a competitive first-team appearance for United, but did make a senior appearance in United's pre-season friendly defeat to AC Milan this summer.

United’s hierarchy were left unsure what triggered his request to leave given he had become a key part of aims in first team training sessions this season.

United were left rocked in September when Gabriel's family unexpectedly requested to cancel his contract with immediate effect.

Daily Mail Sport revealed at the time that United’s hierarchy were left unsure what triggered such a move given he had become a key part of prepares in first team training sessions this season under Michael Carrick.

In a recent development, A week later, Daily Mail Sport revealed that the decline of United since the days of Sir Alex Ferguson was the driving force behind Gabriel's family seeking an exit. United have not won a Premier League title since 2013.

A source close to the family explained that United are 'far away' from the likes of Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, as well as domestic rivals Arsenal and Manchester City, and that they want him to 'learn from the best' to maximise his talents.

'His dad has ambitions for his son to be the best in the world and play with the best and learn from the best and right now that's not current situation at United - far from it,' a source explained.

He has not been seen at the club since he scored a hat-trick for the Under 21s on his UEFA Youth League debut against Sabah.

Russell must do something wacky now after disappointing Bahrain GP qualifying

📅 03 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (4994 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher.
  • It will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together.
  • Russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher. It might even be worth setting your alarm for the 8am UK start time. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen will start in pole position for the first time this year. He will have Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton alongside him.

It will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together. Throw in sweltering temperatures, low grip, high tyre degradation, and the ever-present threat of a Malaysian monsoon sweeping through Sepang, and you have the potential for fireworks.

Russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back. This was a desperately disappointing result for the British driver. After his victory in Baku last weekend, Russell was hopeful he had finally found the winning formula and that he could continue to take the fight to his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, whom he trails in the drivers’ championship by 66pts.

It has been revealed that eighth, four places behind, and 0.24sec slower than the Italian, was not what Russell would have had in mind, although both Mercedes drivers will rise a spot because of the five-place grid penalty meted out to Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar for exceeding his engine allowance for the season.Russell will have felt particularly disappointed as Antonelli only got one run in Q3 after using up a set of soft tyres when he made a mistake and went off track in Q2. He now trails his team mate nine-seven in qualifying head-to-head this year.“No to be honest,” Russell admitted when asked whether he knew why he was so slow. “This circuit is an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the tarmac.“The lap times seven years ago were six or seven seconds faster and at certain points on the track it feels like you are driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone, but it is clearly affecting us more than others.”Mercedes’ lack of performance was doubly unexpected because not only did they arrive here with a massive upgrade package, but Russell revealed this week that he and Antonelli were foregoing the cooling vests you see some drivers sporting on the grid, in favour of car performance.

Toto Wolff, the Mercedes team principal, admitted it was a head-scratcher. “Very difficult to understand,” the Austrian said. “We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is different to all the [other] tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”.

Still, both titles are in the bag so Wolff cannot be too unhappy. Russell is the one who will be really miffed. He really needs to be beating his team-mate pretty much every race weekend if he is to get his title hopes back on track.

At the front, the mood was somewhat different. Verstappen became the first non-Mercedes-powered pilot to take a pole position this year. It was a first pole position for Red Bull Powertrains, too. And with his long run pace looking more than decent, Verstappen should really hold on for his first win of 2026. Hamilton will do his best to hang on to the Dutchman’s coattails. The seven-time champion was delighted when told he had taken P2. “Let’s go guys! Finally! Great job guys, really great job. Car felt great.”.

Recent findings suggest that this was indeed an excellent performance from the Ferrari man – and just the tonic for the Scuderia after weeks of gossip and speculation. Hamilton was admittedly three tenths slower than his rival, which he put purely down to a power deficit on the straights, but he mentioned he was hopeful his long run pace was more competitive. The last time a F1 held a race was held here back in 2017, the British driver claimed pole only to be overhauled by a youthful Verstappen. He will be desperate to turn the tables this time.

“It was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one change before qualifying and we hit the sweet spot,” he reflected afterwards. “I am so, so grateful. I will try my best to hold on to Max tomorrow, and if we are in the fight that would be awesome. I’ve been talking too much, but I guess you talk more when you are happy. It was my best lap of the year. It feels like I won, and I will give it everything tomorrow.”.

Industry observers note that it is Russell, though, who needs a result even more badly if he is to remain a factor in the championship. “As a team, we have yet to have a bad race this whole season and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us,” he admitted, adding that “all the numbers” from the upgrade package suggested it was an improvement on the old car. “But I think there is going to be a lot happening tomorrow. The tyre deg is huge and race pace will be king. So even though today was a real disappointment it is not the be all and end all.”.

Industry observers note that no. 1 ☝️#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/01PqrckQS9.

Tomorrow’s race will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton will start on the front row together. It is a reasonable run down to turn one and there are overtaking opportunities through the first few corners at Sepang, with it being similar to the configuration in China, with plenty of lines and moves on offer.

Respect between two great champions 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/fbZ6aoKRyw.

Sources indicate that “Very difficult to understand. We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is the different to all the (other) tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi [Antonelli], made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”.

On Kimi Antonelli’s track limits breach in Q2:.

“Not good, because Q2 you know you are going to get through. You lose a set [of softs] in a qualifying that is so tight, where we are on the back foot. That is not good.”.

Lewis Hamilton indicates this is the biggest crowd he has ever seen at Sepang, thanking the fans for making it here today. That is actually a bigger compliment than many watching at home may realise. The traffic this weekend has been horrendous. After 10 years without a race in Malaysia, during which time F1 has grown massively, I think they have forgotten how to do traffic management. Shuttles are inconsistent, taxis can’t get in/out, it’s taking forever just to reach the airport a few kilometres away - some fans have been braving the heat and walking. It took over two hours to get back into Kuala Lumpur last night (48km). My understanding is the Bahrainis are organising the race this year, while local forces are handling the traffic outside the circuit.

“The car has been very good since last week. It is good to come back [from his wrist injury] at such a time and I am enjoying it, fighting for the top three. Even though it was not my finest qualifying session it is a good feeling.

“It is a bit unfortunate we take a penalty on a track where we are that fast but, from eighth, I am confident we can come through the field and come back for a good result.”.

Industry observers note that “I love this energy [from the crowd]. Big, big thank you to Malaysia for welcoming us. It is so hot here. I keep saying it, but that has made it a massive challenge for the tyres, the car, the mechanics in the garage. I am really, really thankful to my team. We made so many changes through all these practice sessions. Because the cars are sliding, the tyres are overheating, it was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one last change going into qualifying and I think we hit the sweet spot. To be able to close the gap to two or three tenths to Max [Verstappen], who has been so quick all weekend, is great, and I am so grateful.

Sources indicate that “I am much happier with where the car is, but tomorrow is a completely different ballgame. Making these tyres last around this track, they are overheating from the get-go. Every little bit of wheelspin you have, every little snap you have makes a difference of how far you are going to go. I like to think we have got a good balance. Max was really quick on his long runs, so I will just try my best to hold onto him tomorrow.”.

A reminder that Isack Hadjar will drop from third to eighth after his grid penalty.

QUALIFYING CLASSIFICATIONCan't wait for Sunday! 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/qqi8hPDcKA.

“It is fantastic. We have been trying many grand prix to get pole. Sometimes a bit closer than others but to finally get it, from where we started the season, pretty incredible. I am happy with today and, for sure, I am going to try and win tomorrow. When you start first, that is the target.”.

Industry observers note that substantial disappointment that for Russell. After his win in Baku, where he stated he finally felt hooked up to the car, he was desperate to build the momentum. P8, four places behind Antonelli, was not what he would have had in mind. Has it all to do in the race tomorrow.

Excellent (though not unexpected) pole for Verstappen, and a very good P2 for Hamilton. Could be some fireworks on the front row tomorrow.

*Hadjar’s three-place grid penalty will drop him down to eighth place for the race tomorrow.

Recent findings suggest that neither of the Red Bulls can improve in the first sector but it is those behind them who need significant improvements. The two Ferraris are going along nicely at the start of their final flying laps. Hadjar is unable to improve despite a purple final sector. Verstappen then goes fastest in the final sector and improves his advantage at the top.

According to recent reports, hamilton meanwhile went fastest in the middle sector and goes second fastest overall. Piastri cannot improve but stays ahead of Russell.

Norris is the final man across the line but is only fast enough for P6. That means that Verstappen takes pole in Malaysia, which is the first time this season that Red Bull have taken pole position. Hamilton is second with Hadjar third, although the Frenchman has a five-place grid penalty.

MAX VERSTAPPEN TAKES POLE FOR THE BAHRAIN GRAND PRIX IN MALAYSIA!! 👊#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/NgtaCAZacL.

The two Red Bulls, who are one and two at the moment, will be the first two drivers across the line on these final efforts.

The other nine drivers in Q3 are in the pits so young Antonelli has the track to himself as he sets his one and only flying lap of Q3. He is over four tenths down on Verstappen through the first sector and has plenty of work to do.

According to recent reports, the championship leader sets a decent middle sector where he loses no more time to Verstappen. As it stands he would put himself third before the others do their final runs. He comes across the line in P3 but will have the likes of Hamilton, Piastri, Leclerc, Norris and Russell trying to surpass him.

Russell is the first across the line and sets a time of a 1:36.032. He does not last long at the top as he is immediately displaced by Hadjar, who is half a second quicker.

Hamilton then comes over the line in second, just ahead of his teammate Leclerc. Piastri puts himself between the two Ferraris.

Industry observers note that what about Verstappen? The man who won here the last time we were in Malaysia continues his great form today and goes quickest by more than three tenths.

Antonelli now heads out and will have the track to himself really. This is going to be the championship leader’s only flying lap of Q3.

Russell is the first man to head out for his first flying lap in Q3. Antonelli has remained in the pits with just one fresh set of softs remaining. Verstappen, who right now feels like the favourite for pole, will be one of the last across the line in these first attempts of Q3.

The fight for pole position in Sepang begins now as the green light is on at the end of the pit lane to get Q3 going.

Antonelli, due to that lap time deletion in Q2, has just one newly introduced set of softs for Q3, which could prove costly in his attempts to try and take pole.

Recent findings suggest that P12 the best qualifying result of the season for Alonso. It was only his second time in Q2 after Hungary (P16).

Industry observers note that I should add, P14 was also Lance Stroll’s best qualifying result of the season. His first outing in Q2 this year.

11. Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls)12. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin)13. Carlos Sainz (Williams)14. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)16. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls).

With grid penalties already on their way, neither Colapinto nor Lindblad set lap times in Q2.

In a recent development, verstappen, Leclerc, Piastri, Norris, Hadjar and Russell all remain in the pits. A bit of a risk for Russell down in eighth but his time should be enough to get into Q3.

Lindblad, who will start tomorrow’s race at the back of the grid after penalties, gives his teammate Lawson a tow down the back straight and it works as Lawson just sneaks into the top ten.

According to recent reports, can Bortoleto get back ahead though of Lawson? Yes he can and he will take the final place in Q3. Lawson thought he might be through but the tow was not enough.

Lindblad, who's taking a grid penalty for Sunday's race, gave team mate Lawson a tow but it wasn't quite enough to send the Kiwi into Q3#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/IMlrqg4ENv.

As the young Italian starts his flying lap, there is no-one else out on track so no traffic. He is a lot more cautious at turn six this time than last time, when he had his lap time deleted.

He has not set blistering first and second sector times but a purple final sector puts him into second and the Italian is safely into Q3.

Plenty of other drivers are now heading around the track for their final flying laps of Q2.

11. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)12. Carlos Sainz (Williams)13. Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes)14. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls)15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)16. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin).

Mercedes have put a brand new set of softs onto Antonelli’s car as he heads out promptly, with no lap time to his name so far. Antonelli is still disputing the lap deletion over team radio but his team tell him the images show he exceeded track limits. This is now a lot of pressure on the championship leader; any mistake now and he will not make Q3. His teammate Russell is only in seventh.

Industry observers note that antonelli was fourth fastest but has had his lap time deleted for exceeding track limits at turn six. That is a massive moment in Q2 and could prove problematic if he gets into Q3. Antonelli appeared to be confused when he was told about his lap deletion over team radio but the on-board view looked pretty clear-cut.

Piastri then comes across the line in third.

Here's the moment Kimi ran wide 👀#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/E0VdWdBt8x.

The Dutchman looks in a great spot at the moment to take pole position today and his 1:35.696 is very quick. He is nearly four tenths quicker than Antonelli.

How about the Ferraris? Leclerc was quickest in the middle sector but is nearly three tenths down on Verstappen. Hamilton puts himself into third place. Russell is more than half a second down on Verstappen.

Verstappen has been shown a black and white flag for driving unnecessarily slowly. I doubt he will get a grid penalty for that but it will be a warning for the Dutchman.

Anyway, the drivers, other than Colapinto and Alonso, are on flying laps, with Verstappen presently fastest inthe first sector.

In a recent development, the green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and the second part of qualifying is under way. Like the start of Q1, it is hardly a stampede to go out.

17. Nico Hulkenberg (Audi)18. Oliver Bearman (Haas)19. Esteban Ocon (Haas)20. Alex Albon (Williams)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac).

Recent findings suggest that the Aston Martin of Stroll improves significantly from 20th and is set to make Q2, as is his teammate Alonso. A bit of a surprise to see the Aston Martins improve and make it into Q2.

Go Fernando! 🤩 Go Lance! 🤩First double Q2 appearance this season 🙌#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/xjiWYv6ycr.

Industry observers note that that has seen the Audi of Hulkenberg drop into the drop zone and the German is out. For contrast, his teammate improves to go into eighth place! Hulkenberg had a big lock up into turn 14, which proved very costly.

In a recent development, as it stands, eight of the top nine are remaining in the garage. Russell is in ninth and has not gone out but Gasly above him in eighth has. You would imagine Russell is perfectly safe.

17. Esteban Ocon (Haas)18. Alex Albon (Williams)19. Oliver Bearman (Haas)20. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac).

Ocon, in 17th, is quite far off Hulkenberg in 16th and needs more than four tenths to usurp him.

The screens in the media centre here in Sepang tell me that the air temp right now is 32.8C and the track temp is 58C. It feels even hotter. Lots of chat about cooling vests this week, which are optional. George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he states Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

It’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

“Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he remarked. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external company who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

He added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”.

The two Ferraris are on medium tyres but Leclerc still puts himself into second place. He is then displaced by Hamilton, who slots in behind Verstappen. Good times from the Ferraris on the mediums.

In a recent development, what about the McLarens? Norris goes sixth fastest but is more than six tenths down on Verstappen. Then comes Piastri, who goes fourth fastest, just under four tenths off Verstappen.

Arguably the three favourites for pole; Antonelli, Russell and Verstappen, are all on flying laps.

The first sector goes the way of Verstappen, who is purple, and then the Dutchman goes purple in the middle sector.

Antonelli is two tenths faster than his teammate Russell but Verstappen is over half a second quicker than the Mercedes. Hadjar is then second fastest to show the pace in the Red Bull this weekend.

Industry observers note that most of the teams waited and waited to come out and then suddenly lots of drivers are sent out, resulting in a queue in the pits! With the high track temperatures and high degradation, the drivers are crawling around on their out laps to preserve these soft tyres.

Bumper to bumper in the pit lane! #F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/ff8JO9kB1g.

The two Haas drivers have a free track to themselves whilst everyone else bides their time. In theory, as the hour of qualifying goes on, the track temperature should decrease and the more rubber that is laid down the faster the track should get.

Finally, just before the two Haas drivers finish their first flying laps, the rest of the grid is starting to emerge, led by the Mercedes duo.

Recent findings suggest that the green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and Q1 is officially under way. The two Haas drivers are the first to head out. Other than that, it is a quiet start to Q1.

The top four teams; Mercedes, Red Bull, Ferrari and McLaren, all have a genuine chance of taking pole in Sepang today. I think the true favourites though have to be the Mercedes duo and Max Verstappen but with how close it between all four of the teams you cannot rule anything out.

It is 33 degrees celsius air temperature, with the track temperature up at 58 degrees.

According to recent reports, not long to wait now until qualifying begins. It is hot, humid and dry in Sepang right now. As we know in Malaysia, the weather can change swiftly and thunderstorms can roll in quite quickly but it looks like today’s qualifying will be a dry one. This will be one of if not the hottest qualifying sessions of the season, so much so that we are seeing umbrellas going up to get some shade from the sun rather than sheltering from any rain.

This will be vital to consider after qualifying finishes as there will be some shuffling around:.

Isack Hadjar (Red Bull): five-place grid penalty- latest internal combustion engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): ten-place grid penalty- new engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): five-place grid penalty- causing a collision in BakuArvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls): back of the grid- complete power unit change.

According to recent reports, hadjar has looked good since returning from his wrist injury so could be fighting it out near the front of the grid, although his five-place penalty will drop him down. We know Lindblad will be at the back and is very likely to be joined there by Colapinto, who is not going to be qualifying high up in the top ten in his Alpine.

According to recent reports, haas have confirmed that Frenchman Esteban Ocon will leave at the end of this season. Ocon now faces an uncertain future, with it difficult to see a spot for him on the F1 grid next season. There are suggestions that the 30-year-old’s replacement will be Brazilian Ferrari junior Rafael Camara, although nothing has been confirmed on that front. 21-year-old Camara currently leads the Formula 2 championship.

Industry observers note that TGR Haas F1 Team and Esteban Ocon will part ways at the conclusion of the 2026 season. With plenty of racing ahead, our focus remains on working together to maximize every opportunity through to the final race of the year.#HaasF1 #F1 pic.twitter.com/4iQAuqnSyA.

Recent findings suggest that aston Martin have now confirmed their driver line-up for next season, retaining both Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll. There had been reports that Alonso had been contemplating retirement but the 45-year-old will continue into another season.

Recent findings suggest that aston Martin Aramco confirms Lance and Fernando will continue as the team's drivers in 2027. Read more: ​https://t.co/ePyjJdyAIB pic.twitter.com/VogFUEbNxy.

Other than the second seat alongside Ollie Bearman at Haas, the only other team to keep an eye on is Racing Bulls, with no definite confirmation on their exact driver line-up for next season.

According to recent reports, ferrari this week have publicly backed their team principal Frederic Vasseur, amid speculation over the Frenchman’s position and comments made by former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner, who noted the job at Ferrari would be a “dream job”. Ferrari, who sit second in the constructors’ standings, have not won the drivers’ championship since 2007 (Kimi Raikkonen) and the constructors’ since 2008. Here is a snippet from Tom Cary’s piece on the matter:.

In a hastily convened media call on Tuesday morning, Maria Conti, Ferrari’s chief communication officer, said the Scuderia had decided to issue a vote of confidence in Vasseur in response “not just to the story of Mr Horner, but in general, the speculation about Fred”.

“Ferrari has made its choices,” Conti stated. “We have confidence – full confidence – in Fred Vasseur and in his team, and we continue to do so.

“At this time, it’s really crucial that the team remains united and cohesive, and we are focused with all the energy on the work ahead.”.

It has been revealed that “It is great to be back [in Malaysia]. I am really enjoying the track. We have had some wonderful races here over time. It is actually the 20th time we have been here, it started in 1999, and it is really exciting to be back. I really enjoyed getting out on the track and watching the cars closely.

Recent findings suggest that “The drivers are super fit and they have some cooling but it is not easy. But you almost cannot get enough fluid through your body before your stomach gives up. Having this race and Singapore back-to-back increases that challenge.”.

Especially with the substantial upgrade they have brought this weekend, Mercedes’ lead at the summit is looking unassailable right now.

Almost nine years ago to the day, Max Verstappen took just his second race victory in Formula 1. Lewis Hamilton, who took pole position, and Daniel Ricciardo joined Verstappen on the podium. Despite being nine years ago, plenty of drivers still on the grid were racing that weekend. Here they are and who they were racing for:.

Max Verstappen (Red Bull) Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes) Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes) Esteban Ocon (Force India)Nico Hulkenberg (Renault)Sergio Perez (Force India)Fernando Alonso (McLaren)Lance Stroll (Williams)Carlos Sainz (Toro Rosso)Pierre Gasly (Toro Rosso).

With Russell winning in Baku and Antonelli finishing fifth, the latter’s championship lead was cut to 66 points. If Russell is going to usurp his teammate, he is going to need a few more similar results to last weekend due to the size of Antonelli’s lead. If Antonelli were to suffer a retirement, then that completely changes the outlook.

Formula One returns to Malaysia for round 16 of the season for the Bahrain Grand Prix. That probably sounds strange but after the Bahrain Grand Prix was originally postponed in March, F1 reinstated it to the calendar with Malaysia hosting it because of the ongoing war in the Middle East. Despite being held in Malaysia, Bahrain have retained the naming rights for the event, which is officially known as the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The last time Formula One was in Malaysia was nine years ago back in 2017, when a young whippersnapper named Max Verstappen, still four years away from winning his first world championship, claimed just his second victory.

Last time out around the streets of Baku, Mercedes’ George Russell claimed victory at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, pipping Verstappen by just a tenth of a second. That was Russell’s first grand prix win since June and cuts his team-mate Kimi Antonelli’s lead in the drivers’ standings to 66 points. Antonelli had a challenging weekend in Baku, starting 16th after a crash in qualifying and coming home in fifth to see his championship lead to Russell cut by 15 points.

Verstappen was quickest in first practice yesterday, with the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc fastest in second practice. Earlier today, championship leader Antonelli was nearly three tenths clear of the field in third practice. Mercedes, 160 points clear at the top of the constructors’ standings, have brought significant upgrades this weekend, which includes a newly introduced floor, rear suspension and rear corner. It is the team’s first significant car patch since the Canadian Grand at the end of May.

This race in Malaysia represents the second leg of the season’s first flyaway triple header, with the Singapore Grand Prix to come next weekend, so the demands on the teams and the drivers are incredibly high. Qualifying from Sepang gets under way at 9am (GMT).

Falkirk vs St Johnstone - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Anthony Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 03:57, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 05:20.
  • Fighting for a spot in the top half of the Scottish Premiership, promoted St Johnstone will lock horns with in-form Falkirk at Falkirk Stadium on Saturday.
  • The Bairns are eyeing a sixth win on the bounce, while the Saints could go four games unbeaten this weekend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 03:57, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 05:20.

Fighting for a spot in the top half of the Scottish Premiership, promoted St Johnstone will lock horns with in-form Falkirk at Falkirk Stadium on Saturday.

The Bairns are eyeing a sixth win on the bounce, while the Saints could go four games unbeaten this weekend.

John McGlynn's Falkirk are the form team in the Scottish top flight over the past five games, and they will be confident of earning maximum points yet again on home turf.

The latest in their string of triumphs was a 5-2 demolition of last term's runners-up Hearts at Tynecastle Park, where the Bairns raced into a 4-0 lead by the half-time interval.

Bolstering the magnitude of McGlynn's side's feat further is the fact that thrashing followed a 2-0 win against Celtic, which itself marked a third consecutive clean sheet.

All in all, taking 15 points from the last 15 on offer has put Falkirk third in the Scottish Premiership, though their 21-point tally leaves them six behind second-placed Rangers and 10 short of top-of-the-table Celtic.

On the other hand, the Bairns are now four points clear of their seventh-placed opponents, and boasting the second-best defensive record in the division, McGlynn will be optimistic about his team's chances of seeing extending that advantage.

Meanwhile, St Johnstone earned promotion to the top flight by winning the Scottish Championship last term, and while plenty of sides have struggled with the step up in the past, Simo Valakari's men are in a strong position.

The Saints are right now seventh with 17 points after 13 games, level with sixth-placed Dundee United and fifth-placed Dundee.

Prior to the international break, Valakari's side downed the Dee 2-1, taking an early lead via Josh Campbell before Kai Fotheringham won the clash roughly 20 minutes from time.

That victory ended a four-game run without a win, though St Johnstone had only tasted defeat once during that stretch, and arrive with just a single loss from their last seven outings overall.

The visitors will be the underdogs on Saturday, but buoyed by their resilience - as well as having scored more goals (17) than any other team in the bottom half - they are sure to fight for the chance to climb into the top six.

Falkirk Scottish Premiership form:.

St Johnstone Scottish Premiership form:.

Falkirk will be without injured full-backs Ryan Strain and Leon McCann, though Jack McMillan and Scott Tanser should be on hand to start either side of centre-halves Lewis Neilson and Liam Henderson.

At the opposite end of the pitch, right wingers Aodhan Doherty and Joseph Gardner are dealing with respective foot and thigh injuries, while the left-sided Ethan Laidlaw and attacking midfielder Aidan Nesbitt have ankle issues to contend with.

In their absence, Jacob Murrell looks set to start up top, supported by Ethan Ross, Finley Barbrook and Owen Eames.

As for St Johnstone, they have a generally fit squad, with centre-back Bozo Mikulic reportedly available after breaking his nose against Dundee just 14 minutes into his return from 20 months out with an ACL injury and a slew of concerns in the aftermath.

Elsewhere, Joel Cotterill could operate alongside Jason Holt in the centre of the park, flanked by wing-backs Liam Smith and Josh Campbell.

Falkirk possible starting lineup:.

Bain; McMillan, Neilson, Henderson, Tanser; Spencer, Melniks; Ross, Barbrook, Eames; Murrell.

St Johnstone possible starting lineup:.

Steward; Diabate, Finlayson, Alic; Smith, Cotterill, Holt, Campbell; Steven, Schmidt, Fotheringham.

In the midst of more than just a purple patch, Falkirk have been immense of late, hammering Hearts, beating Celtic and maintaining a strong defensive record.

St Johnstone have proven their own resilience since making the step back up to the Premiership, but they will be hard-pressed to hold out against the division's form team.

AC Milan are looking at possible options to come in and replace Luka Modric, with one name emerging as the preference.

In a recent development, as TMW report, Gerry Cardinale is ready to invest further in Milan. The goal is to build an increasingly stronger team, taking advantage of the various transfer windows to grow gradually. The ultimate goal must be to return to fighting for a Scudetto, which the Rossoneri have not won since 2021-22.

The priority remains a central defender, with Gonçalo Inacio in pole position. An investment of at least €40m will be required, assuming the Portuguese club is willing to part with him mid-season. Alternatives include Union Saint-Gilloise’s Sylla, Lens’ Ganiou and Borussia Dortmund’s Reggiani.

However, the report goes on to mention a task that will need to be tackled ahead of next season, given that Modric’s deal is set to expire and it is at the moment unknown if he will retire.

Milan must think about who the Croatian should hand the reins to, and the ‘favourite’ is VfB Stuttgart star Angelo Stiller. The initiative is to acquire a top midfielder who is similar in mould but can still grow.

The task of acquiring him will be entrusted to the latest Head of Football Markus Krösche, who will officially be in office starting from January, but in reality is already planning future moves.

He seems gravitated towards a target that Milan’s scouts have had in their sights for at least a couple of seasons anyway, and that is Stiller. The 25-year-old is also a key member of the German national team right now coached by Jurgen Klopp.

The massive temptation also comes from the fact he has a €40m release clause, and Krösche knows him well given his past in the Bundesliga. That said, other ideas such as Brighton’s Ayari and Bournemouth’s Scott shouldn’t be overlooked yet either.

Tech Report: PSG transfer news: Paris ready to open door to January departure

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (430 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 20 Nov 2026 06:29.
  • It has been revealed that lucas Chevalier wants to leave Paris Saint-Germain in the next winter transfer window.
  • Having joined PSG in the summer of 2025 from Lille for £34m (€40m), Lucas Chevalier has failed to make his mark at the Parisian club.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 20 Nov 2026 06:29.

It has been revealed that lucas Chevalier wants to leave Paris Saint-Germain in the next winter transfer window. The Parisian club are ready to let him go on one condition.

Having joined PSG in the summer of 2025 from Lille for £34m (€40m), Lucas Chevalier has failed to make his mark at the Parisian club. While he was expected to succeed Gianluigi Donnarumma, he now finds himself as a mere understudy to Matvey Safonov.

The Russian goalkeeper has won his place as first choice and is not letting go of it. Paris are very pleased with his performances and have reportedly even secretly wrapped up a contract extension. Safonov has played every game for the two-time European champions this season, leaving Lucas Chevalier without any game time.

It is a difficult situation for the French international, who missed the last World Cup and has not been called up by new France manager Zinedine Zidane.

According to recent reports, already mentioned as a possible departure last summer, the former Lille man had chosen to stay. Canal+ reports that PSG had told him he would get a fresh chance if he kept working.

However, that chance never came. A point of no return appears to have been reached. ‘He wants to play, he needs to play. Today, his wish is to look elsewhere to find game time’ - Gauthier Kuntzmann revealed on the Late Football Club show. The Parisian club are ready to let him leave this winter.

‘Paris Saint-Germain are aware that the situation of Lucas Chevalier cannot drag on. On top of that, he is losing market value and that is a factor, even if everything is going very well financially at PSG. 'I am telling you, Paris Saint-Germain do not rule out the idea, even in the short term, of seeing Lucas Chevalier leave on loan or in a sale, it will depend on the offers’ - Philippe Carayon explained on the same show.

The task does not look simple for Lucas Chevalier. ‘Finding a goalkeeper position at a good club in January will not be simple. Except in the event of an injury at a club’ - Alain Roche warned. In any case, in this saga, PSG will only let their goalkeeper leave on one condition.

Industry observers note that ‘There will be an absolute prerequisite for Paris Saint-Germain, which is to find a top-level replacement for Safonov’ - Philippe Carayon stressed. That could complicate a departure for the French goalkeeper in January 2027 even further.
